title: K Smallest Pairs From Two Arrays
description:
Given two sorted integer arrays `nums1` and `nums2`, return the `k` pairs with the smallest sums.
Each pair consists of one element from `nums1` and one element from `nums2`. For a pair `[nums1[i], nums2[j]]`, its sum is `nums1[i] + nums2[j]`.
Return up to `k` pairs with the smallest sums. If there are fewer than `k` possible pairs, return all available pairs.

title: Restaurant Ordering and Pricing System
description:
Design an object-oriented restaurant ordering and pricing system. The system should support multiple types of menu items, with `Pizza` as one of the core items. A pizza consists of a `Crust`, a `Size`, and zero or more `Topping` objects. Each crust has a base price, each size has a price multiplier, and each topping has its own price.
The pizza price should be calculated as `Price = (base_price + sum(toppings_prices)) * size_multiplier`.
The design should be extensible so that new sizes, toppings, or menu item types can be added without modifying the existing pricing and ordering logic. The system should also use appropriate object-oriented principles to separate responsibilities and avoid hard-coded conditional logic.

title: Find Duplicate Files by Content
description:
Given an absolute root path, recursively traverse all files under the directory. Files are considered duplicates when their complete contents are identical, regardless of file name, file extension, or file path. Group files with identical contents together and return all groups, including groups containing only one unique file.
The input provides two helper functions: `listFolder(path)` returns all items directly under the current path, and `isFolder(path)` determines whether a path is a directory. The solution should recursively traverse the directory tree, generate a content signature for each file, and group files with the same signature.
The key engineering requirement is that large files should not be fully loaded into memory. A production-quality solution should use file size as an initial filter, calculate hashes incrementally with streaming reads, and optionally perform byte-level comparison when files have the same size and hash.

title: Maze Shortest Path
description:
Given a maze represented as a 2D grid, where an empty space `' '` represents a walkable cell and `'X'` represents an obstacle, find the shortest number of steps from a given start position to a given destination position.
You can move between adjacent walkable cells in four directions: up, down, left, and right.
Return the minimum number of steps required to reach the destination. If the destination cannot be reached, return the corresponding failure value defined by the interviewer.
The maze should be treated as an unweighted graph, where each walkable cell represents a node and each valid movement represents an edge with equal cost.

title: Restaurant Ordering System Design
description:
Design a restaurant ordering and pricing system that supports different types of menu items. A Pizza consists of a crust, a size, and zero or more toppings. The system should calculate the final price dynamically while remaining easy to extend when new sizes, toppings, crusts, or menu item types are introduced.
The initial pricing formula is:
`Price = (base_price + sum(toppings_prices)) × size_multiplier`
The design should avoid hard-coded strings and primitive values for domain concepts such as size, crust, and toppings. The system should also support additional menu items such as Pasta through a common `MenuItem` abstraction.

title: Binary Logistic Regression and Multiclass Gaussian Generative Model
description:
You are given a feature matrix `X` containing continuous-valued samples and a label vector `y`.
Part 1: Binary Classification
Assume `y` contains two classes, `0` and `1`. Build a parameterized logistic regression model and implement the parameter estimation procedure using Maximum Likelihood Estimation. The implementation should compute the sigmoid function, binary cross-entropy loss, and gradients, then optimize the model parameters using gradient descent.
Part 2: Multiclass Classification
Assume `y` contains multiple classes such as `0`, `1`, and `2`. Build a Gaussian generative classifier that models the class prior probability and the conditional distribution of each feature given a class. Estimate the model parameters from the training data and use the resulting posterior probabilities to predict the class of new samples.
The implementation should not rely on high-level machine learning libraries such as `sklearn`. Use basic mathematical operations and numerical computation primitives. The implementation should also consider numerical stability, including probability underflow, exponential overflow, and zero variance.

title: Network Delay Time
description: You are given a directed, weighted graph representing a network. Starting from node `k`, determine the minimum time required for a signal to reach every node. If there is at least one node that cannot be reached from `k`, return `-1`. Otherwise, return the maximum of the minimum travel times to all nodes.

title: Circular Necklace Split
description:
Given a circular necklace represented by a string `necklace`, each character is either `D`, representing a diamond, or `R`, representing a ruby.
Find two cut positions that divide the circular necklace into two continuous parts such that both parts contain exactly the same number of diamonds and the same number of rubies.
Return the two cut positions as `[start, end]`. The first part contains the characters encountered from `start` to `end` in clockwise order, and the remaining characters form the second part.
If no valid split exists, return an empty array.
The solution should efficiently handle a large necklace and avoid unnecessary duplication of the circular string.

title: Merge Two Sparse Time Series
description:
You are given two sparse time series, A and B. Each time series consists of events represented as (timestamp, value). The events in each series are sorted by timestamp in strictly increasing order.
Each event means that starting from its timestamp, the corresponding series changes to the given value and keeps that value until the next event. Before the first event of a series, its value is assumed to be 0.
Merge the two time series into one chronological sequence where each output event represents the sum of the current values of A and B.
The output must be compressed: only record a timestamp when the combined value actually changes. If both sequences contain an event at the same timestamp, both updates must be applied atomically before calculating the combined value.
The merged result must continue until all events from both sequences have been processed, including the case where one sequence ends earlier than the other. The final events must correctly preserve the last known value of the exhausted sequence.

title: Two Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer target, find two distinct elements in the array whose values add up to target.
Return the indices of the two elements whose sum equals target.
You may assume that each input contains exactly one valid solution, and the same element cannot be used twice.
The goal is to solve the problem using a single pass through the array with efficient lookup rather than checking every possible pair.

title: Reorganize String
description:
Given a string s containing lowercase English letters, rearrange its characters so that no two identical characters are adjacent.
Return any valid rearrangement of the string if one exists.
If no valid rearrangement is possible, return an empty string.
A valid rearrangement must use every character from the original string exactly once.
A valid arrangement exists only when the frequency of the most common character does not exceed (n + 1) / 2, where n is the length of the string. This condition provides an early mathematical check for impossible inputs.

title: Design and implement a user browsing history system
description:
Design and implement a user browsing history system for an e-commerce website.
The system records the products that users have recently viewed and maintains their browsing history in order from most recently viewed to least recently viewed.
The system should support the following operations:
A user can view a product. If the product is already in the user's browsing history, it should be moved to the most recently viewed position.
A user can retrieve their recent browsing history.
Each user's browsing history has a fixed capacity. When the capacity is exceeded, the least recently viewed product should be removed.
The system must support multiple users, and each user's browsing history must remain independent from other users.
The core data structure should provide O(1) average-time lookup and O(1) update of browsing order.

title: Design a Pizza Ordering System
description:
Design a pizza ordering system that allows customers to create pizzas, add pizzas to an order, apply coupons, and calculate the final price.
The system should represent individual pizzas with their names, base prices, and ingredients. An order should maintain the pizzas selected by the customer and calculate the subtotal and final total.
The system should also support different types of coupons. Different coupon types may apply discounts according to different business rules, such as percentage discounts, fixed-amount discounts, buy-one-get-one offers, free-item offers, or minimum-spend discounts.
The design should be extensible so that adding a new coupon type does not require modifying the core Order logic.
The final order price must never be negative.

title: Design a Log Stream Processor to Find the Most Active User
description:
Design a log stream processor for a messaging application. Each incoming log event represents a message sent from one user to another and contains four fields: timestamp, sender_username, receiver_username, and message_text.
Implement a RegisterEvent(timestamp, sender_username, receiver_username, message_text) method to register a message event and a GetMostActiveUser() method to return the user with the highest number of active conversations.
A conversation is defined as a unique pair of users who have exchanged messages. Regardless of how many messages are sent between the same two users, the pair counts as only one conversation for each user. A conversation is counted for both participants, even if only one participant sends a message.
For example, if Alice sends 100 messages to Bob, they still have only one conversation. If Alice also exchanges messages with Charlie and David, Alice has three unique conversation partners.
The system should process incoming events incrementally and maintain the most active user efficiently, without scanning every user whenever GetMostActiveUser() is called.

title: Count Islands in a Binary Tree
description:
Given a binary tree in which each node contains either 0 or 1, determine the total number of islands in the tree.
An island consists of one or more nodes with value 1 that are connected through direct parent-child relationships. Two nodes with value 1 belong to the same island if there is a path between them consisting entirely of nodes with value 1.
A node with value 0 separates islands. If a node with value 1 has a parent whose value is 0, or if the node is the root, it starts a new island.
The tree is acyclic, and connectivity is defined only through parent-child relationships. The solution should count each island exactly once and should avoid unnecessary auxiliary data structures when possible.

title: Currency Conversion Path Optimization
description:
Given a set of currency exchange rates, design a system that converts an amount from a source currency to a target currency through one or more intermediate currencies.
Each exchange rate represents a directed conversion edge. For example, if 1 USD can be exchanged for 0.92 EUR, the graph contains an edge from USD to EUR with an exchange rate of 0.92.
The system should support finding a valid conversion path between two currencies. During the interview, the interviewer may introduce additional requirements, such as minimizing the number of exchanges or maximizing the final converted amount.
Different optimization objectives require different algorithms. Finding any valid path does not guarantee the minimum number of exchanges or the maximum converted amount.
The implementation should clearly distinguish between these objectives and handle unreachable currencies appropriately.

title: Binary Tree Subtree Sum
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, update each node's original value to the sum of all values in its subtree, including the node itself. Return the total sum of the entire tree.
A subtree consists of a node and all its descendants. For each node, its final value must equal its original value plus the original values of all nodes in its left and right subtrees.
The tree should be updated in place. The key requirement is that each node's final value must represent its complete subtree sum rather than merely the sum of its immediate children.
The solution should use post-order traversal, processing the left subtree and right subtree before updating the current node. It must also account for highly skewed trees, where recursive call-stack usage can reach O(n).

title: Merge Multiple Binary Trees and Calculate Subtree Sums
description:
Given an array containing k binary tree roots, merge the trees into a new binary tree by adding the values of nodes at corresponding positions. If a position contains a node in some trees but is empty in others, use the values of the existing nodes.
After merging the trees position by position, update every node in the resulting tree so that its value equals the sum of all values in its subtree, including itself.
The final result must be a new binary tree. The algorithm must perform both operations correctly: position-wise aggregation across the input trees and bottom-up subtree-sum aggregation.
For example, simply adding corresponding node values is insufficient. The resulting merged tree must subsequently aggregate the values of all descendants into their ancestors.
The solution should handle null roots, asymmetric tree structures, and highly skewed trees. It should also consider whether merging and subtree-sum calculation can be combined into one recursive traversal.

title: Basic Toy Programming Language Interpreter
description:
Design and implement a basic interpreter for a toy programming language. The interpreter receives a list of string instructions, processes them in order, and returns the final value of a single integer register x, initially set to 0.
The interpreter supports five instructions:
ADD n: Add the integer n to the current value of x.
MULTIPLY n: Multiply the current value of x by the integer n.
DEF fname: Begin defining a function named fname. Instructions following DEF belong to the function body and must be stored rather than executed immediately.
END: Finish the current function definition and register its body so that it can be executed later.
EXEC fname: Execute the previously defined function fname by processing its stored instructions in order.
Function definitions cannot be nested. The input instructions are assumed to be syntactically valid under the basic problem constraints. However, function bodies may invoke other previously defined functions, potentially creating recursive or indirect function calls.
The interpreter must distinguish between definition mode and execution mode. Instructions inside a function definition should not modify x until that function is explicitly executed through EXEC.
For a robust implementation, also consider undefined function calls, unmatched DEF/END instructions, recursive execution cycles, and excessive call depth.

title: Weighted Random Task Prioritizer with Removal
description:
Design and implement a task prioritization system that maintains a pool of tasks, each associated with a positive integer weight.
The system must support two operations:
addTasks(tasks, weights): Add multiple tasks and their corresponding weights to the task pool. Each task must be paired with the weight at the same index.
popTasks(count): Randomly select and return the requested number of tasks according to their weights. A task with weight w should have a probability of w / totalWeight of being selected at each draw.
Sampling must be performed without replacement. Once a task is selected, it must be immediately removed from the pool, and its weight must be subtracted from the remaining total weight. Subsequent selections must use the updated pool and remaining weights.
The task pool does not need to preserve its original order. This allows the implementation to optimize removal by replacing the selected element with the last element and removing the last element.
The implementation should maintain the total weight incrementally rather than recalculating it for every selection. It should also validate input arrays, positive weights, requested counts, and potential integer overflow.

title: Product of Array Except Self
description:
Given an integer array nums, return an array answer such that answer[i] is equal to the product of all elements of nums except nums[i].
You must solve this problem without using the division operator and achieve O(n) time complexity.
The solution should avoid creating additional prefix and suffix arrays. Instead, use the output array to store intermediate prefix products and a single rolling variable to accumulate suffix products.
The algorithm must correctly handle arrays containing zero values. It should also consider the potential for integer overflow when the input values are large.

title: Find the Most Liked Content
description:
Given a list of like events, identify the content ID that has received the highest number of likes.
Each event contains a userId representing the user who initiated the like and a contentId representing the video or content being liked. Count the number of like events associated with each contentId and return the content ID with the highest total count.
Content IDs must be represented as strings to support identifiers such as UUIDs and Base64 strings rather than assuming they are integers.
If multiple content IDs have the same maximum number of likes, return the lexicographically smallest content ID to ensure deterministic results.
If the input is null, empty, or contains no valid events, return null.
The basic implementation counts every valid like event, including repeated likes from the same user. An optional deduplication mode can be added when the business requirement specifies that each user may like a given content item only once.

title: Unique Product Views Analysis
description:
Given a collection of viewing log records, each containing a customer_id and a product_id, identify the customer who has viewed the largest number of distinct products.
Each customer may view the same product multiple times, but repeated views of the same product by the same customer should count only once. Different customers viewing the same product should be counted independently.
Return the customer ID with the highest number of distinct products viewed. If multiple customers have viewed the same maximum number of distinct products, return the lexicographically smallest customer ID.
If the input is empty, null, or contains no valid records, return null.

title: Valid Parentheses
description:
Given a string s containing only the characters '(', ')', ', ', '[' and ']', determine whether the input string is valid.
A string is valid if every opening bracket is closed by a bracket of the same type, brackets are closed in the correct order, and every closing bracket has a corresponding opening bracket.
The matching pairs are '()' , '' and '[]'.
Return True if the string is valid and False otherwise.

title: Next Greater Element
description:
Given an integer array nums, find the next greater element for every element in the array.
The next greater element of nums[i] is the first element to the right of index i that is strictly greater than nums[i]. If no such element exists, return -1 for that position.
Return an array result where result[i] contains the next greater element of nums[i].

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
description:
Given an integer array nums that was originally sorted in strictly increasing order and then rotated at an unknown pivot, search for a target value.
The array contains no duplicate elements.
Return the index of target if it exists in nums. Otherwise, return -1.
The solution must achieve O(log n) time complexity.

title: String to Double Conversion
description:
Implement a function that converts a numeric string into a double-precision floating-point number without using built-in conversion functions such as Double.parseDouble() or Double.valueOf().
The input string may contain leading or trailing whitespace, an optional positive or negative sign, an integer part, a decimal point, and a fractional part.
The parser must process the characters manually, validate the input format, and return the corresponding numerical value.
If the input contains invalid characters, multiple decimal points, only a sign, or no numeric digits, reject the input.

title: Daily Temperatures
description:
Given an integer array temperatures representing the daily temperatures, return an integer array answer where answer[i] is the number of days you have to wait after the i-th day to get a warmer temperature.
If there is no future day with a higher temperature, answer[i] should be 0.
A warmer temperature must be strictly greater than the current temperature.

title: Selling Partner Promotions - Maximum Concurrent Promotions
description:
Given a list of promotions, where each promotion is represented by a start time and an end time, determine the maximum number of promotions that are active simultaneously at any point in time.
Each promotion is represented as [startTime, endTime]. A promotion becomes active at its start time and stops being active at its end time.
Return the maximum number of concurrent promotions.
The goal is to efficiently determine the maximum overlap among all promotion intervals.
For this implementation, assume that promotions use half-open intervals [startTime, endTime). A promotion ending at time t is no longer active when another promotion starts at time t. Therefore, end events must be processed before start events at the same timestamp. If the original interview specifies different endpoint semantics, the event ordering must be adjusted accordingly.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
description:
Given an integer array nums, return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
A subsequence is a sequence that can be derived from an array by deleting some or no elements without changing the order of the remaining elements.
A strictly increasing subsequence requires every element to be greater than the previous element. The selected elements do not need to be contiguous in the original array.
The solution should achieve O(n log n) time complexity for large inputs.

title: Social Network Shortest Path
description:
Given an undirected, unweighted social network graph and two user profile identifiers, startProfile and targetProfile, find the shortest path connecting the two users through their friend relationships.
The graph is represented as an adjacency list, where each user is associated with a list of their direct friends.
Return the complete shortest path as a list of profile identifiers, including both the starting user and the target user.
If no path exists, return an empty list.
If the starting profile and target profile are the same, return a list containing that profile.

title: Selling Partner Promotions - Maximum Concurrent Promotions
description:
Given a list of promotions, where each promotion is represented by a start time and an end time, determine the maximum number of promotions that are active simultaneously at any point in time.
Each promotion is represented as [startTime, endTime]. A promotion becomes active at its start time and stops being active at its end time.
Return the maximum number of concurrent promotions.
The original interview material also discusses soft limits and hard limits. A soft limit is an elastic threshold that may be exceeded under permitted circumstances, while a hard limit is an absolute threshold that must not be exceeded. The core algorithmic task is to calculate the maximum concurrent promotion count.
For this implementation, assume promotions use half-open intervals [startTime, endTime). If one promotion ends at the same timestamp that another begins, they are not considered active simultaneously.

title: Next Highest Rated Movie Finder
description:
Given a list of movies, where each movie contains a name and an integer rating, find the first movie to the right of each movie whose rating is strictly greater than the current movie's rating.
For each movie, return its name and the name of the first subsequent movie with a higher rating. If no such movie exists, return "none".
The output should preserve the original order of the movies.

title: Longest Increasing Consecutive Path in a Matrix
description:
Given an m × n integer matrix, return the length of the longest consecutive increasing path in the matrix.
You may start from any cell and move only in four orthogonal directions: up, down, left, and right. Diagonal movement is not allowed.
For a path to be valid, every next cell must contain a value exactly one greater than the current cell. In other words, matrix[nextRow][nextCol] == matrix[currentRow][currentCol] + 1.
Each move must remain within the matrix boundaries. The path may start and end at any cell.

title: Super Add Function - Arbitrary-Precision String Addition
description:
Implement a function that adds two non-negative integers represented as strings and returns their exact sum as a string.
The input integers may contain far more digits than standard integer types can represent. You must not convert the entire input strings into built-in integer types or use an arbitrary-precision integer library. Instead, simulate ordinary column-wise addition, processing digits from right to left and propagating the carry.
The implementation should support operands of different lengths, handle a final carry, normalize leading zeros, and return the result without unnecessary leading zeros. If an operand is null, empty, or contains non-digit characters, the implementation should reject the input according to a clearly defined validation policy.
The core algorithm supports non-negative integers. Supporting negative numbers and subtraction is an extension rather than a requirement of the basic problem.

title: Employee Interest Matching
description:
Given a list of employees, each containing an employee ID, name, interests, and a history of employees they have already met, implement a function that finds employees who share at least one common interest with a specified target employee but have never met that employee.
The function should return the IDs of all eligible employees. The target employee must not appear in the results, and employees who have already met the target employee must be excluded.
The original problem does not specify a required output order, so any order is acceptable unless the interviewer provides an additional constraint.

title: Maximum Concurrent Promotions
description:
Given a list of promotions, where each promotion is represented by a start time and an end time, determine the maximum number of promotions running simultaneously and return a time point when this maximum occurs.
Each promotion is represented as (startTime, endTime). Convert every promotion into two events: a start event that increases the active promotion count and an end event that decreases it.
Sort the events chronologically and scan them while maintaining the current number of active promotions. Track the maximum count and the corresponding time when this maximum is first reached.
If multiple time points have the same maximum concurrency, return the earliest time point according to the event ordering.

title: Extensible Log Processor with Pluggable Extractors
description:
Design a generic log processing system that accepts a collection of log lines and a configurable list of extractors.
The processor should parse each log line into a structured LogEntry and pass the parsed entry to every registered extractor. Each extractor examines the entry and updates a shared metrics structure when the entry matches its specific condition.
The initial requirements are to support two extractors:
1. Database Error Counter: Count the number of database error log entries.
2. Agent Abandoned Call Counter: Count how many times each agent has an abandoned call.
The log processor should return the aggregated metrics rather than relying on global variables. New extractors should be registerable without changing the core processing loop.
The original interview material does not specify an exact log format. For the implementations below, assume each line uses this pipe-delimited format:
timestamp|service|level|agent|event
For example:
2026-10-20T10:00:00|database|ERROR|agentA|query_failed
A database error is defined as service = database and level = ERROR. An abandoned call is defined as event = call_abandoned, with the corresponding agent identifier available in the log entry.

title: Nth Most Productive Driver
description:
Given an array where each element represents the number of packages delivered by a driver, find the Nth most productive driver based on the number of packages delivered.
The goal is to identify the Nth largest delivery count without necessarily sorting the entire array.
The optimal approach uses the QuickSelect algorithm. QuickSelect partitions the array around a pivot so that elements with larger delivery counts appear before elements with smaller delivery counts. It then continues searching only the partition containing the target rank.
For this implementation, N is 1-indexed, and duplicate delivery counts occupy separate ranking positions. Since the input contains only delivery counts and no driver IDs, the function returns the Nth largest delivery count. If the interviewer requires the actual driver, each element should instead contain both a driver identifier and a delivery count.

title: Singleton Pattern Implementation
description:
Implement the Singleton design pattern to ensure that a class has only one instance throughout the program's lifetime and provides a globally accessible point of access to that instance.
The implementation should prevent external code from directly constructing additional instances. It should also address concurrent access when multiple threads attempt to retrieve the instance simultaneously.
A key requirement is to avoid recursively creating new instances inside the constructor. Instance creation should be controlled by the singleton access mechanism.
For modern C++, a function-local static object is the recommended default solution because C++11 guarantees thread-safe initialization of local static variables. A mutex and double-checked locking are alternative approaches, but double-checked locking requires careful memory-ordering and initialization guarantees.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Matrix
description:
Given an m × n integer matrix, find the length of the longest strictly increasing path. You may start from any cell and move up, down, left, or right to an adjacent cell, but each move must lead to a strictly greater value. Diagonal movement is not allowed.
The goal is to return the maximum number of cells in any valid strictly increasing path.
The optimal approach uses Depth-First Search (DFS) with memoization. For each cell, calculate the longest increasing path starting from that cell and store the result in a memoization matrix. If a cell has already been processed, reuse its cached result instead of exploring the same paths again.

title: Skill Detector for Game Combos
description:
Design and implement a SkillDetector class for an action game. The system maintains a history buffer of player inputs and detects whether the most recent input sequence matches any predefined skill combination.
Each skill is associated with a skill ID and an ordered sequence of button inputs. Whenever a new button input arrives, the detector appends it to the input buffer and checks whether the buffer ends with any registered skill sequence.
If one or more skills match, collect and return all matching skill IDs, then immediately clear the input buffer to begin a new matching process. If no skill matches, retain the input history so subsequent button presses can complete a skill combination.
The matching logic should support skills with different sequence lengths. If multiple skills match the same input sequence, the detector should return all matching skills unless an explicit priority rule is introduced.

title: Count Unique Grid Pattern Paths
description:
Given a grid with R rows and C columns, count the number of distinct valid pattern paths that can be drawn by moving between grid cells.
A path can start at any cell. At each step, the next cell must be horizontally or vertically adjacent to the current cell. Diagonal movement is not allowed, and each cell can be visited at most once within a path.
The solution uses Depth-First Search (DFS) with backtracking. Start from every cell, mark it as visited, and recursively explore all valid unvisited neighbors. Each non-empty path represents a valid pattern and contributes one to the total count. After exploring a path, unmark the current cell so it can be used in other paths.
The original requirements do not specify a minimum path length, so this implementation counts paths of every length from 1 through R × C. Paths are treated as ordered sequences, meaning a path and its reverse count as two different patterns. If the interviewer intends to count them as the same pattern, additional deduplication is required.

title: Door Passing Problem
description:
Given n people who need to pass through a single door, each person has an arrival time and a direction. Passing through the door takes exactly one second, and only one person can pass through the door at a time.
Each person's direction is represented as 0 for entering and 1 for exiting. When both entering and exiting queues contain people, the following priority rules apply:
1. If the door was used for entering during the previous second, entering has priority.
2. If the door was used for exiting during the previous second, exiting has priority.
3. If the door was not used during the previous second, exiting has priority by default.
If only one direction has waiting people, a person from that direction passes through the door.
Return an array indicating the exact second at which each person passes through the door. The output order must match the original input order.
The solution uses simulation with two queues. People are processed in arrival-time order and placed into either the entering queue or the exiting queue. At each second, the algorithm selects the next person according to the priority rules, records their passing time, and updates the previous direction. When both queues are empty but some people have not arrived, the clock jumps directly to the next arrival time, and the default exiting priority is restored.

title: Door Passing Problem
description:
Given n people who need to pass through a single door, each person has an arrival time and a direction. Passing through the door takes exactly one second, and only one person can pass through the door at a time.
Each person's direction is represented by 0 for entering and 1 for exiting. When both entering and exiting queues have waiting people, the following priority rules apply:
1. If the door was used for entering during the previous second, entering has priority.
2. If the door was used for exiting during the previous second, exiting has priority.
3. If the door was not used during the previous second, exiting has priority by default.
Given the arrival times and directions of all people, return an array containing the exact time each person passes through the door. The result must preserve the original input order.
The solution uses simulation with two queues. People are processed in arrival-time order and placed into the appropriate queue. At each second, the algorithm selects a person according to the priority rules, records the passing time, and updates the previous direction. When both queues are empty but people have not yet arrived, the clock jumps directly to the next arrival time, and the previous direction resets to exiting.

title: Phrase Search V2 — Document Phrase Search
description:
Implement a document search system that supports searching for words and identifying documents containing a specified phrase. The system uses a DP class to represent a word's position within a document and a Cursor interface to traverse and locate matching positions.
The system should support multiple documents, with each document containing indexed words and their positions. A document position is represented by its document ID and word position.
Implement the core cursor operations, including get, advance, isValid, and seek, so callers can inspect the current position, move to the next position, check whether the cursor remains valid, and efficiently jump to a target position.
The system should also implement printDocIds to identify and output the document IDs containing the requested word or phrase. For phrase search, all query words must appear in the same document at consecutive word positions and in the specified order.
The design should separate document-position representation, cursor traversal, and phrase-matching logic to make the implementation reusable and extensible.

title: K-Window Element Removal
description:
Given two integer lists, list1 and list2, and an integer K, define the K-window of a list as the set of distinct elements appearing in its first K positions.
Remove the minimum number of elements from list2 so that the K-window of the modified list2 has no elements in common with the K-window of list1.
The K-window is determined by the first K positions, not by the first K distinct elements. Duplicate values count as separate positions, even though the K-window itself is a set.
The goal is to preserve as many elements as possible while ensuring that the first K elements of the resulting list contain no value belonging to the K-window of list1.

title: Find the Next Right Node at the Same Depth
description:
Given the root of a tree and a reference to a target node, return the reference to the next node immediately to its right at the same depth as the target node.
If the target node is the rightmost node at its depth, return null.
The tree is not necessarily a binary search tree, so the solution cannot rely on comparing node values to determine the target's location.
The recommended solution uses breadth-first search (BFS) to traverse the tree level by level. At each level, process the nodes in left-to-right order. When the target node is encountered, return the next node in that level if one exists. Otherwise, return null.

title: Elevator Control System
description:
Implement the main control loop for a single elevator that operates between floors 0 and 5.
The elevator receives a collection of floor requests and must decide which direction to move, when to stop, and when to reverse direction. The elevator should follow an improved SCAN scheduling strategy, serving requests in its current direction before reversing to handle requests in the opposite direction.
The elevator must move exactly one floor at a time. After each movement, it checks whether the current floor has a pending request. If so, it stops at that floor and removes the request from the pending set.
The implementation must also handle an empty request list. When there are no pending requests, the elevator should remain idle rather than continuing to move unnecessarily.
For this reference implementation, each request represents a floor that the elevator must visit. All requests are known when scheduling begins, and multiple requests for the same floor can be served by a single stop.

title: Prime Calendar - Internal Event Calendar System
description:
Design and implement an internal event calendar system called Prime Calendar.
The system should support three core operations:
1. Add an event with a title, date, start time, and end time.
2. Check whether a new event conflicts with an existing event on the same date.
3. Retrieve all events scheduled for a given date.
An event should contain four fields: title, startTime, endTime, and date.
The initial implementation can store all events in a vector and scan the collection to check for conflicts. However, this approach becomes inefficient as the number of events grows.
Improve the design by organizing events in a map keyed by date, with a sorted set of events for each date. This allows the system to locate a day's events efficiently and check for conflicts without scanning the entire calendar.
For this solution, assume events use half-open time intervals [startTime, endTime), so an event ending at 10:00 does not conflict with another event starting at 10:00. Also assume that conflicting events cannot be added and that the calendar stores events on a single date rather than events spanning multiple dates.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return its sum.
A contiguous subarray consists of consecutive elements from the original array. The array may contain positive numbers, negative numbers, and zeros.

title: Majority Element
description:
Given an integer array nums, determine whether a strict majority element exists. A strict majority element is an element that appears more than half the total number of times in the array.
Return the majority element if one exists. Otherwise, return an empty Optional value.
The input is described as an array of caller IDs. The algorithm must correctly determine whether any ID occurs strictly more than half the time.

title: Prime Video Watch History and Recommendation System
description:
Design and implement a video recommendation system that supports adding videos to a catalog, recording users' viewing history, and recommending unwatched videos that belong to genres the user has previously watched.
The system should maintain video metadata, associate each user with their viewing history, and return recommendations based on the user's watched genres. Videos already watched by the user must be excluded.

title: Phrase Search V2 (Proper Stubs)
description:
Implement a phrase search system using a prebuilt word-position index, a DocumentPosition class, and a Cursor interface.
The system must support two search operations:
Single-word search: Find all unique document IDs containing a specified word.
Two-word phrase search: Find all unique document IDs containing two specified words at adjacent positions in the correct order.
The cursor provides access to indexed word occurrences and supports operations such as checking validity, retrieving the current position, advancing, and seeking directly to a target position.
The implementation should avoid unnecessarily processing every occurrence within a document when a match has already been found. For phrase search, the two cursors should coordinate their positions to determine whether the second word immediately follows the first word in the same document.

title: Find Employees with the Highest Salary
description:
Given an Employee table containing the columns id, name, age, and salary, write a query to return the names and salaries of all employees who have the highest salary.
The query must handle cases where multiple employees share the highest salary. All employees tied for the maximum salary must be returned.

title: Optimize a Payment Verification System
description:
Design and optimize a payment verification system that processes a large number of payment requests. Each payment must pass multiple verification rules, and some rules require database queries to retrieve settlement instructions.
The system should improve throughput and reduce latency while maintaining correctness and data consistency.
The proposed optimization strategy includes:
1. Processing independent payment requests concurrently using a bounded thread pool.
2. Caching frequently accessed settlement instructions using an LRU cache.
3. Grouping database lookups into batch queries to reduce network round trips.
4. Using database connection pooling efficiently.
5. Handling concurrent payment processing without introducing duplicate or inconsistent updates.
The exact payment rules, database schema, traffic volume, and measured performance targets were not specified in the interview record. Implementations should therefore treat rule evaluation and database access as replaceable components.

title: Top-K Frequent Products
description:
Implement a system that tracks product purchase frequencies and returns the top K most frequently purchased products.
The system must support two operations:
1. purchase(item_id): Record a purchase of the specified product and increment its purchase frequency by one.
2. get_top_k(k): Return the K products with the highest purchase frequencies. If multiple products have the same frequency, their relative order does not matter.
The initial implementation should prioritize correctness and efficient frequency tracking. Further optimization should consider the relative frequency of purchase operations and top-K queries, as well as the trade-offs between heaps, ordered data structures, lazy updates, and caching.

title: Personal Library Management System
description:
Design and implement a personal library management system that allows users to organize books across multiple shelves. Each book contains a title and author, and each shelf is identified by a unique shelf ID and a description.
The system must support the following operations:
- Add a shelf using its unique ID and description.
- Place a book on a specified shelf.
- Find the shelf locations of a particular book.
- Check whether the library contains a particular book.
- Support multiple copies of the same book, including copies stored on different shelves.
The implementation should use appropriate data structures to support efficient book lookup and location retrieval. The design should remain simple and extensible.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more elements without changing the relative order of the remaining elements. The selected elements do not need to be contiguous.
The subsequence must be strictly increasing, meaning each element must be greater than the previous element.

title: Word Search II
description:
Given an m*n character board and an array of strings `words`, find all words that can be formed by connecting adjacent cells horizontally or vertically.
Each cell can be used at most once in a single word. Diagonal movements are not allowed.
Return all words from `words` that can be found on the board. Unless explicitly required, words of any length are valid, including single-character and two-character words.

title: Construct Binary Tree from Preorder and Inorder Traversal
description:
Given two integer arrays, `preorder` and `inorder`, representing the preorder and inorder traversals of a binary tree, reconstruct and return the original binary tree.
- Preorder traversal visits the root first, followed by the left subtree and then the right subtree.
- Inorder traversal visits the left subtree first, followed by the root and then the right subtree.
- All node values are unique.
- The tree is not necessarily a binary search tree.
The key observation is that the first element of the preorder traversal is always the root. Its position in the inorder traversal determines how the remaining elements are divided between the left and right subtrees.

title: Voice Ordering System: Hierarchical Menu Search and Fuzzy Matching
category: Data Structures and Algorithms / Object-Oriented Design
description:
Implement the core matching component of a voice ordering system. The system receives a user's spoken request as text and searches a hierarchical menu to find the most appropriate menu item.
The menu consists of a `Menu`, which contains multiple `MenuGroup` objects. Each `MenuGroup` can contain both `MenuItem` objects and nested `MenuGroup` objects. The hierarchy may contain circular references, so the implementation must prevent infinite traversal.
The system must support two search modes:
- Exact matching: Find a menu item whose name exactly matches the query.
- Fuzzy matching: When the speech recognition result is inaccurate, find the top K menu items with the smallest edit distance from the query.
The implementation should handle empty inputs, avoid infinite recursion, and use an efficient data structure to maintain the top K results without storing every candidate.

title: Employee Time Tracking System: Calculate Total Work Hours in the Last 7 Days
category: Data Structures and Algorithms / Object-Oriented Design
description:
Design and implement an employee time-tracking system that records clock-in and clock-out timestamps and calculates each employee's total working hours over the previous seven days.
The system must support three main operations:
- `clockIn(employeeId, timestamp)`: Record when an employee starts working.
- `clockOut(employeeId, timestamp)`: Record when an employee finishes working and save the completed work interval.
- `calculateHoursForEmployee(employeeId, now)`: Calculate the employee's total working hours within the rolling seven-day window ending at `now`.
Employees may work across midnight, so a work session's start and end timestamps may fall on different calendar days. The calculation must use actual elapsed time rather than weekday names or calendar-day counting.
The system should also support multiple employees, reject invalid clock-in and clock-out sequences, and remove obsolete records to prevent unnecessary storage growth.
For this implementation, only completed work sessions contribute to the calculated total. The rolling window is defined as the interval from `now - 7 days` to `now`, and only the portion of a work session overlapping that interval is counted.

title: Meeting Rooms II — Minimum Number of Meeting Rooms
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals, where each interval contains a start time and an end time, determine the minimum number of meeting rooms required to accommodate all meetings without conflicts.
Two meetings can use the same room if the first meeting ends at or before the second meeting starts. Meetings that overlap in time must use separate rooms.
The solution should efficiently track ongoing meetings and release rooms when meetings finish.

title: Meeting Rooms II
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals, where each interval contains a start time and an end time, determine the minimum number of meeting rooms required to accommodate all meetings without overlapping.
A meeting room can be reused when a previous meeting ends at or before the next meeting starts.
If a meeting has the same start and end time, it has zero duration and does not require a room.

title: Flood Fill
description:
Given an \\(m \times n\\) integer matrix `image`, where each element represents the color of a pixel, along with starting coordinates `sr` and `sc` and a new color `color`, perform a flood fill operation.
Starting from `image[sr][sc]`, change the color of the starting pixel and all pixels connected to it through the four directions (up, down, left, and right) that have the same original color to the specified new color.
Return the modified image.
A pixel is considered connected if it can be reached from the starting pixel by moving through adjacent pixels of the same original color. Diagonal connections do not count.

title: String Mathematical Expression Evaluator
description:
Given a string representing a mathematical expression containing single-digit numbers from `0` to `9`, their English word representations (`zero` through `nine`), and addition or subtraction operators, evaluate the expression and return the result.
The expression may contain both numeric and word-based operands, as well as symbolic and word-based operators (`+`, `-`, `plus`, `minus`).
Requirements:
- Support addition and subtraction only.
- Each operand must represent a single digit from `0` to `9`.
- Each pair of operands must be separated by exactly one operator.
- Validate the expression before evaluating it.
- Return `None` for invalid input.

title: Check if it is Possible to Split Array
description:
Given an integer array `nums` of length `n` and an integer `m`, determine whether it is possible to split the original array into single-element subarrays through a sequence of splitting operations.
In each operation, select a contiguous subarray of length at least two and split it into two non-empty contiguous subarrays. Both resulting subarrays must satisfy at least one of the following conditions:
- The subarray has a length of exactly one.
- The sum of its elements is greater than or equal to `m`.
Return `true` if the entire array can eventually be split into single-element subarrays; otherwise, return `false`.
The key challenge is to determine whether a valid splitting sequence exists without exploring every possible partition.

title: String Compression
description:
Given a string, implement a compression algorithm that compresses consecutive occurrences of the same character only when the number of occurrences is greater than or equal to 4.
The compressed format must be `count x character`, where `count` is the number of consecutive occurrences, followed by the character `x`, and then the repeated character itself.
If a group contains fewer than 4 consecutive occurrences, preserve the original characters without compression.
After processing the entire string, return the compressed string only if it is strictly shorter than the original string. Otherwise, return the original string.

title: Rotate Image
description: Given an n × n 2D matrix representing an image, rotate the image 90 degrees clockwise in place. The original matrix must be modified directly, and no additional matrix may be allocated to store the rotated result.

title: Median of Two Sorted Arrays
description:
Given two sorted integer arrays, `nums1` and `nums2`, return the median of the two sorted arrays combined.
The solution should avoid explicitly merging the arrays and aim for logarithmic time complexity by using binary search or an efficient kth-element selection algorithm.
If the combined array has an odd number of elements, return the middle element. If it has an even number of elements, return the average of the two middle elements.

title: High Priority Queue with FIFO Ordering
description:
Design and implement a high-priority queue that supports two operations:
- `put(key, priority)`: Insert an element with the specified priority.
- `get()`: Remove and return the element with the highest priority currently in the queue.
The priority queue must satisfy the following requirements:
- A larger numerical value represents a higher priority. Priority `0` is the lowest priority.
- Elements with the same priority must be processed in first-in, first-out (FIFO) order.
- Do not use Java's built-in `PriorityQueue` or other built-in priority queue implementations. Implement the necessary heap and circular queue data structures yourself.
- Support dynamic capacity growth when the circular queue becomes full.
- If the queue is empty, `get()` should return an empty result rather than attempting to remove an element.

title: Median Salary Across Multiple Departments
description:
Given employee salary records from multiple departments, calculate the median salary across all employees. Each employee record is represented as a string containing the salary, name, and position in the format `$salary:name:position`.
For example, `$190,000:Alice:Software Engineer` represents an employee with a salary of $190,000.
The input consists of multiple department employee lists. When there are exactly two departments, their employee records are already sorted by salary in ascending order. The solution should take advantage of this ordering rather than sorting the records again.
For two departments, use a two-pointer approach to find the median without merging the entire lists. For three or more departments, collect the salaries, sort them, and calculate the median.

title: Expression Calculator with Operator Precedence and Parentheses
description:
Implement a calculator that evaluates a mathematical expression represented as a string. The expression contains integers, the four arithmetic operators (`+`, `-`, `*`, `/`), parentheses, and optional whitespace.
The calculator must respect standard arithmetic precedence: multiplication and division have higher precedence than addition and subtraction. Parentheses override the default precedence and must be evaluated first. Integer division must truncate toward zero.
The implementation should correctly handle nested parentheses, mixed operators, negative intermediate results, and whitespace. A recursive descent parser or a two-stack algorithm can be used to evaluate the expression.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
description: Given an integer array nums, find the contiguous subarray with the largest sum and return that sum. The subarray must contain at least one element.

title: Whitelist Full Coverage Validation
description:
Given a collection of numeric-string suffixes used by a whitelist, determine whether the configured suffix rules cover every possible decimal-string user ID.
A user ID is accepted if its string representation ends with at least one configured suffix. Build a trie by inserting each suffix in reverse character order.
During validation, a trie node is considered fully covered if it is a terminal node, because a configured suffix has already matched. Otherwise, all ten digit branches from 0 through 9 must exist and must themselves be fully covered.
Assumption: User IDs are treated as strings, so leading zeros are significant. The original interview notes do not specify a fixed user-ID length. If the intended domain uses fixed-length IDs or excludes short IDs, the validation rule must be adjusted accordingly.

title: Move Zeroes
description:
Given an integer array nums, move all zeros to the end of the array while maintaining the relative order of all non-zero elements.
The operation must be performed in-place without creating another array.

title: Coin Change Combinations
description:
Given an array of distinct positive coin denominations and a target amount, find all possible combinations of coins whose total value equals the target.
Each denomination can be used an unlimited number of times. Different orderings of the same collection of coins are considered the same combination.
For example, if the available denominations are `[1, 2]` and the target is `4`, the valid combinations are:
- `[1, 1, 1, 1]`
- `[1, 1, 2]`
- `[2, 2]`
The task is to enumerate all valid combinations, not merely return their count.

title: First and Last Non-Repeating Character Indices
description:
Given a string `s`, find the index of the first non-repeating character and the index of the last non-repeating character. A character is non-repeating if it appears exactly once in the string.
Return both indices as a pair. If no non-repeating character exists, return `-1`. If the string is empty, return `-1`.

title: Coin Change
description:
Given an integer array `coins` representing different coin denominations and an integer `amount` representing a target amount, return the minimum number of coins needed to make up that amount.
If the amount cannot be formed using the given coin denominations, return `-1`.
You may use each coin denomination an unlimited number of times.

title: Thread-Safe Singleton Pattern
description:
Implement a thread-safe Singleton class in Java that guarantees only one instance of the class is created, even when multiple threads attempt to access it concurrently.
The implementation should use double-checked locking to avoid unnecessary synchronization after the instance has been initialized.
The solution must ensure that:
- Only one instance of the class is created.
- Multiple threads can safely access the instance.
- Synchronization is performed only when the instance has not yet been initialized.
- The implementation prevents visibility issues and instruction reordering during instance initialization.

title: Maze Path Finding
description:
Given an `m x n` maze represented by a two-dimensional integer array, determine whether a ball can travel from a given starting position to a destination.
Each cell contains either `0` or `1`:
- `0` represents an open cell.
- `1` represents a wall.
Following the movement rules of LeetCode 490, the ball moves in one of four directions and continues rolling until it hits a wall or the boundary of the maze. It cannot stop voluntarily in the middle of an open corridor.
Return `true` if the ball can stop at the destination; otherwise, return `false`.

title: Employee Directory System
description:
Design and implement an Employee Directory System to manage employees and their reporting relationships within an organization.
The system should support the following operations:
- AddEmployee: Add a new employee to the directory.
- RemoveEmployee: Remove an employee from the directory and update related reporting relationships.
- GetDirectReports: Retrieve the direct reports of a specific employee.
- GetEmployee: Retrieve an employee's information by employee ID.
- UpdateEmployee: Update an employee's information, including their name and manager.
Each employee has a unique employee ID, a name, an optional manager ID, and a list of direct reports.
The implementation should use traditional Java syntax without Stream API or Lambda expressions.
When removing an employee, their direct reports should be reassigned to no manager (`null`). The employee should also be removed from their own manager's direct reports list.

title: Binary Tree Maximum Path Sum
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, return the maximum path sum of any non-empty path.
A path is a sequence of nodes connected by parent-child edges. A path may start and end at any nodes in the tree, but each pair of adjacent nodes in the sequence must be directly connected. A node cannot appear more than once in the same path.
The path does not have to pass through the root. Node values can be positive, zero, or negative.
The goal is to find the maximum possible sum of all node values along a valid path.

title: Clone Graph
description:
Given a graph represented by a Graph object containing a collection of vertices, implement a function that returns a completely independent deep copy of the graph.
Each Vertex contains a data value and a list of references to its neighboring vertices. The Graph object maintains a collection of all vertices.
The cloned graph must preserve the original graph's structure, including all vertices and edges. No cloned vertex should reference an original vertex. The solution must correctly handle cycles, self-loops, and disconnected components.

title: Interval Union
description:
Given two sorted lists of non-overlapping intervals, return their union as a sorted list of non-overlapping intervals.
Each interval is represented by a start value and an end value. The input lists are already sorted by start value, so there is no need to sort all intervals again.
The union must include every point covered by either input list. When intervals overlap, merge them into one interval. Otherwise, preserve them as separate intervals.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description:
Given an integer array nums and an integer k, return the kth largest element in the array.
The kth largest element is defined by its position in the sorted order, not by the number of distinct elements. Duplicate values must be counted separately.
Your solution should achieve an average time complexity better than O(n log n), where n is the length of the array.

title: Binary Tree Boundary Traversal (Clockwise)
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, return its boundary nodes in clockwise order, starting with the root.
The clockwise boundary consists of the following parts:
1. The root node.
2. The right boundary, traversed from top to bottom, excluding leaf nodes.
3. All leaf nodes, collected from right to left.
4. The left boundary, traversed from bottom to top, excluding leaf nodes.
Each boundary node should appear only once in the result.

title: Shortest Path in a Maze with Direction Bitmasks
description:
Given a two-dimensional integer matrix representing a maze, find the minimum number of steps required to travel from a start position to an end position.
Each cell contains a bitmask representing the directions in which movement is allowed:
- North: 8 (binary 1000)
- East: 4 (binary 0100)
- South: 2 (binary 0010)
- West: 1 (binary 0001)
A movement is allowed only if the corresponding bit is set in the current cell's value. For example, a cell with value 10 (binary 1010) allows movement north and south.
Return the minimum number of steps required to reach the destination. If no valid path exists, return -1.
Each move to an adjacent cell costs one step. Movement permissions are determined by the current cell's bitmask; the problem does not require the destination cell to have the opposite direction bit set.

title: Number Guessing Game
description:
Implement a number guessing game in which the computer randomly generates an integer between 1 and 10, inclusive. The player has at most three attempts to guess the target number.
After each guess, the program should provide feedback:
- If the guess is smaller than the target, print "Too low!".
- If the guess is greater than the target, print "Too high!".
- If the guess matches the target, print "You have the right answer!" and terminate the game immediately.
If the player fails to guess the target within three attempts, print a game-over message and reveal the correct number.
The implementation should separate guess evaluation from game-flow control. The maximum number of attempts should be configurable to support future extensions.

title: String to Integer (atoi)
description:
Implement the `myAtoi` function that converts a string into a 32-bit signed integer.
The conversion must follow these rules:
1. Ignore leading whitespace characters.
2. Check for an optional `+` or `-` sign and determine the number's sign.
3. Read consecutive digits until a non-digit character is encountered or the end of the string is reached.
4. If no digits are parsed, return `0`.
5. If the resulting integer exceeds the 32-bit signed integer range, clamp it to the nearest boundary:
- Maximum: \(2^{31}-1=2147483647\)
- Minimum: \(-2^{31}=-2147483648\)
The solution must handle overflow during parsing rather than converting the entire numeric substring directly.

title: Meeting Rooms II
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals `intervals`, where each interval is represented as `[start, end]`, determine the minimum number of conference rooms required to accommodate all meetings without conflicts.
Two meetings can use the same room if the first meeting ends at or before the second meeting starts.
The intervals may not be sorted initially. Your solution should efficiently determine the minimum number of rooms required.

title: Number of Visible People in a Queue
description:
Given an array `heights` representing people standing in a queue, where each person faces the same direction, return an array `answer` such that `answer[i]` represents the number of people that person `i` can see to their right.
A person at index `i` can see a person at index `j` if:
- `i < j`.
- Every person between them is shorter than both people at indices `i` and `j`.
A taller person can block the view of people behind them. However, a person taller than the current person can still be visible as the first taller person in that direction.

title: Collatz Conjecture — Number of Steps to Reach One
description:
Given a positive integer `n`, repeatedly apply the following rules until the number becomes `1`:
- If `n` is even, divide it by `2`.
- If `n` is odd, multiply it by `3` and add `1`.
Return the number of iterations required to reach `1`.
This sequence is known as the Collatz sequence. The Collatz conjecture states that every positive integer eventually reaches `1`, although this has not been proven for all positive integers.

title: Shortest Unsorted Continuous Subarray
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the shortest continuous subarray that, if sorted in ascending order, makes the entire array sorted in ascending order.
Return the length of this shortest subarray. If the array is already sorted, return `0`.

title: As Far from Land as Possible
description:
You are given an `R × C` grid where `grid[i][j] = 1` represents land and `grid[i][j] = 0` represents water.
Find the water cell whose distance to its nearest land cell is the greatest, and return that distance.
The distance between two cells is their Manhattan distance:
\[
|r_1-r_2|+|c_1-c_2|
\]
Only horizontal and vertical movements are allowed. Diagonal adjacency does not count as a direct connection.
If the grid contains only land or only water, return `-1`.

title: Find Two Points Whose Connecting Line Divides the Remaining Points Equally
description:
Given a list of points in a two-dimensional plane, find two points such that the line passing through them divides the remaining points equally between its two sides.
A point is considered to be on the left or right side of the line based on the sign of the cross product. Points lying exactly on the line are excluded from both counts.
Return the 1-based indices of any pair of points that satisfies the condition. If no valid pair exists, return `null` or an equivalent empty result.

title: Search a 2D Matrix II
description: Given an m × n integer matrix in which each row is sorted in ascending order from left to right and each column is sorted in ascending order from top to bottom, determine whether a target value exists in the matrix. Return `true` if the target is found; otherwise, return `false`.

title: Remove Duplicates from a 2D Array While Preserving Order
description: Given a two-dimensional integer array, remove all duplicate elements across the entire array while preserving the original order of the first occurrence of each element. Each element should appear at most once in the output. Preserve the relative order of the remaining elements and their original row grouping. If a row contains no remaining elements after deduplication, omit that row from the result.

title: Merge Three Sorted Arrays and Remove Duplicates
description: Given three sorted integer arrays A, B, and C, merge them into a single array containing all distinct elements in ascending order. Duplicate values may appear within an individual array or across multiple arrays, but each value must appear only once in the result. Since the input arrays are already sorted, the solution should take advantage of their ordering to avoid sorting the combined result again.

title: Check Whether an Element Appears More Than N/4 Times
description:
Given a sorted integer array nums of length \\(n\\), where \\(n\\) is divisible by 4, determine whether any element appears strictly more than \\(n/4\\) times. Return `true` if at least one element satisfies this condition; otherwise, return `false`.
Since the array is sorted, all occurrences of a particular value form a contiguous range. We can exploit this property to determine the frequency of candidate values efficiently using binary search.

title: First Element Greater Than K in a Sorted Array
description:
Given a sorted array of integers `arr` and an integer `K`, find the index of the first element that is strictly greater than `K`. If no such element exists, return `-1`.
The array is sorted in ascending order, and the solution should efficiently locate the leftmost element greater than `K` without traversing the entire array.

title: Design a Battleship Game System
description:
Design a two-player Battleship game system. Each player has a 10 × 10 grid and a fleet consisting of three ships: a Submarine of length 3, a Battleship of length 4, and an Aircraft Carrier of length 5. Each player takes turns attacking a coordinate on the opponent's grid. An attack results in either a hit or a miss. A ship is considered sunk when all its cells have been hit. The first player to sink all the opponent's ships wins the game.
The system should manage ship placement, board states, attack tracking, turn switching, and winner determination. The design should separate responsibilities across classes and provide consistent method return values.

title: Cheapest Flights Within K Stops
description:
You are given `n` cities numbered from `0` to `n - 1` and an array `flights`, where `flights[i] = [from, to, price]` represents a flight from city `from` to city `to` with ticket price `price`.
Given a source city `src`, a destination city `dst`, and an integer `k`, find the cheapest price from `src` to `dst` with at most `k` stops. If no valid route exists, return `-1`.
A stop is an intermediate city between the source and destination. Therefore, a route with at most `k` stops can contain at most `k + 1` flights.

title: Peak Network Load Over Time
description:
Given session data for an internet service provider, each session contains a user ID, a start time, an end time, and a bandwidth usage value. A user may have multiple sessions throughout the day.
Find the maximum cumulative bandwidth usage across all simultaneously active sessions and return the time window during which this peak load occurs.
Each session is represented as `[user_id, start_time, end_time, speed]`. Assume sessions use half-open intervals `[start_time, end_time)`, meaning a session is active at its start time but no longer active at its end time.
If multiple time windows achieve the same maximum load, return the earliest one. If there are no sessions, return a peak load of `0` with no time window.

title: Kth Largest Element in an Array
description:
Given an unsorted integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, find the kth largest element in the array.
The kth largest element is defined by its position in sorted descending order, not as the kth distinct element. Duplicate values count as separate elements.
You should aim to solve the problem efficiently without fully sorting the entire array.

title: Count Univalue Subtrees
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, count the number of univalue subtrees.
A univalue subtree is a subtree in which every node has the same value. A single-node subtree is considered a univalue subtree because all of its nodes have the same value.
We can solve the problem using depth-first search (DFS) with postorder traversal. Each recursive call determines whether the subtree rooted at the current node is univalue. If it is, we increment a counter.
Note on the source material: the supplied notes contain inconsistent statements about the first example's expected output and the tree's node values. The examples below use the concrete tree structures from the provided Java code, for which the expected outputs are consistent with the algorithm.

title: Most Frequent Three-Page Sequence in User Visit Logs
description:
Given a list of page-view logs, where each log contains a timestamp, a user UUID, and a page name, find the three-page sequence that occurs most frequently across all users.
A three-page sequence consists of three consecutive page visits by the same user, ordered chronologically. Each user's visits must be processed independently, and sequences from all users contribute to the global frequency count.
Return the most frequently occurring three-page sequence and its frequency. If no user has at least three page visits, return None or the equivalent empty result. If multiple sequences have the same maximum frequency, clarify the tie-breaking rule with the interviewer.

title: Optimal Watchtower Height to Maximize Profit
description:
Given N houses located at coordinates (x, y) and a watchtower at a fixed location (A, B), determine the optimal height of the tower to maximize profit.
A house can be monitored by the tower if its Euclidean distance from the tower is less than or equal to the tower's height. Each monitored house pays a fixed amount C, while the construction cost is H per unit of tower height.
The profit is calculated as:
Profit = Number of Monitored Houses × C − Tower Height × H
Return the tower height that maximizes profit. If building a tower does not produce a positive profit, return 0.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence (LIS)
description:
Given an integer array `nums`, find the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.
A subsequence is a sequence that can be derived from an array by deleting some or no elements without changing the relative order of the remaining elements. The subsequence does not need to be contiguous.
Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: E-commerce Shipping Cost Calculator with Tiered Pricing
description:
Design a shipping cost calculator that supports different shipping rates for different countries and tiered pricing for individual products.
Each country has its own shipping configuration. Each product's configuration contains multiple pricing tiers, where each tier specifies a minimum quantity, an exclusive maximum quantity, and a unit price.
For example, the first two units may cost 1000 each, the third and fourth units may cost 950 each, and the fifth unit onward may cost 900 each.
The minimum quantity is inclusive, and the maximum quantity is exclusive. Quantity positions are zero-based, so the range `[0, 2)` covers the first two units.
Given a country, an order containing product IDs and quantities, and a shipping configuration, calculate the total cost by applying the appropriate pricing tiers to each product.

title: JavaScript Event Loop and Asynchronous Execution
description:
Given a JavaScript code snippet containing synchronous statements, setTimeout, and Promise, determine the execution order of the statements and explain why they execute in that order.
The problem evaluates understanding of JavaScript's asynchronous execution mechanism, including the call stack, microtask queue, and macrotask queue.

title: CSS Selector Specificity and Priority
description:
Given an HTML element that matches multiple CSS selectors, each defining a different background color, determine which style will ultimately be applied.
