Explain how CSS specificity works and how the browser determines which declaration takes precedence.

title: JavaScript this Keyword and Binding Mechanism
description:
Given a JavaScript object containing a method that references `this`, determine how the value of `this` changes when the method is called directly versus when it is extracted into an independent function.
Explain how JavaScript determines the value of `this` based on the function invocation pattern.

title: JavaScript let vs var in Loops and Closures
description:
Given a `for` loop containing `setTimeout`, compare the output when the loop variable is declared using `let` versus `var`.
Explain how block scope, function scope, and closures affect the values captured by asynchronous callbacks.

title: Autocomplete System Using Trie (Prefix Tree)
description:
Design an autocomplete feature for the Waymo application. Given a list of possible destination names and a user's partial input, return all destinations that start with the given prefix.
The initial approach can use linear search with the `startswith()` method. However, the system needs to support millions of destinations, so the solution should be optimized for large-scale data and real-time autocomplete queries.
The goal is to implement an efficient prefix-search mechanism using an appropriate data structure.

title: Longest Duplicate Substring
description:
Given a string s, find the longest substring that appears at least twice in the string. The repeated occurrences are allowed to overlap. Return any one of the longest duplicate substrings. If no duplicate substring exists, return an empty string.
The challenge is to efficiently identify duplicate substrings without repeatedly creating and hashing every possible substring. The solution should optimize both substring-length searching and hash calculation.

title: Count Ordered Pairs Satisfying a[i] - a[j] = i - j
description:
Given an integer array a, count the total number of ordered pairs (i, j) satisfying the following condition:
a[i] - a[j] = i - j
An ordered pair means that (i, j) and (j, i) are considered two different pairs. Self-pairs (i, i) are also valid because they always satisfy the condition.
The goal is to first understand the brute-force solution and then optimize it using mathematical transformation and a HashMap.

title: Split Square Cakes Into Two Equal Areas Using Binary Search
description:
Given a collection of square cakes placed on a 2D coordinate plane, each with a specified position and side length, find a horizontal cutting line (a Y-coordinate) that divides the total cake area into two equal parts.
The cutting line must ensure that the total area below the line equals half of the total area.
The problem can initially be solved using binary search over the Y-coordinate range. However, the interviewer expects further optimization to avoid repeatedly calculating the area of every square.
The key challenge is to efficiently calculate the area below a candidate horizontal line and optimize the solution when the coordinate range is large but the number of squares is small.

title: Matrix Diagonal Printing
description:
Given a two-dimensional integer matrix, print all elements in diagonal order.
Each diagonal should be printed on a separate line, with elements separated by spaces.
The traversal direction is diagonally down and left: move one row down and one column left (row + 1, col - 1).
Use a two-phase traversal strategy:
1. Start from every column in the first row.
2. Start from every remaining row in the last column.
Ensure that every matrix element is visited exactly once without duplication or omission.

title: Longest Increasing Path in a Binary Tree
description:
Given a binary tree, find the length of the longest strictly increasing path.
A path consists of nodes connected through parent-child relationships. It can start at any node in the tree but must move downward from a parent to one of its children.
A path is strictly increasing if every child node has a value greater than its parent.
Return the maximum number of nodes in any valid increasing path.
This is a variation of LeetCode 298, Binary Tree Longest Consecutive Sequence. Unlike the original problem, consecutive values do not need to differ by exactly one.

title: Payment Data Cleaning and Analysis
description:
Given a payment transaction dataset, perform six data manipulation tasks using Python Pandas.
The tasks cover basic filtering, missing-value analysis, aggregation, refund calculations, date analysis, and conditional feature creation.
The six tasks are:
1. Filter records from July 2025 where payment_amount > 0.
2. Identify missing values and calculate their percentages.
3. Group transactions by party_id and calculate total payment amount and payment count.
4. Calculate refund percentages for each payment_method.
5. Find the first and last payment dates for each account.
6. Create a binary indicator where time_on_book <= 3 identifies a new account.
The interviewer focuses on practical Pandas proficiency, clean implementation, and the ability to explain each transformation.

title: Credit Card Payment Return Prediction – Binary Classification
description:
Machine Learning – Credit Card Payment Return Prediction
Given a historical credit card payment dataset, build a binary classification model to predict whether a payment will be returned.
The target variable is return_flag:
- 0: Payment is successful and not returned.
- 1: Payment is returned.
The objective is to build a predictive model, perform feature engineering, handle class imbalance, select an appropriate classification algorithm, tune hyperparameters, and evaluate model performance.
The interviewer particularly focused on understanding why Random Forest might be preferred over Logistic Regression, how XGBoost should be trained, and what happens internally during GridSearchCV.

title: SQL Roll Rate Analysis – Monthly Delinquency Transition Matrix
description:
Given a loan account dataset containing daily account records, calculate the overall monthly roll rate between different delinquency buckets.
Each account may have multiple records within a month. First, identify the latest available record for each account in each month. Then classify each account into one of five delinquency buckets based on its days_delinquent value.
The five delinquency buckets are:
Bucket	Days Delinquent
0	Current (0 days)
1	1–29 days
2	30–59 days
3	60–89 days
4	90+ days
Finally, compare consecutive monthly snapshots for each account and calculate the number and percentage of transitions between delinquency buckets.
The interviewer specifically clarified that the expected result is an overall roll rate matrix, not a separate matrix for each reporting month. Vintage analysis is not required.

title: Longest Color-Ordered Path in a Forest Grid – DFS + Backtracking + Bitmask
description:
Given a 2D grid representing a forest, each cell contains one of five colors: G, Y, O, R, or B.

Find the length of the longest valid path satisfying the following conditions:
1. The path must start from any cell containing G.
2. Colors must follow the order G → Y → O → R → B.
3. Moving between cells of the same color is allowed multiple times.
4. Movement is allowed in all eight directions, including diagonals.
5. Each cell can be visited at most once.
6. A valid path must contain all five colors. Otherwise, return 0.
The objective is to maximize the number of visited cells while satisfying all constraints.

title: Design an Autocomplete System Using Trie
description:
Design an autocomplete system for a customer support platform that manages support categories.
The system must implement four core operations:
1. Insert: Add a new category.
2. Search: Check whether a complete category exists.
3. Suggest: Return all categories matching a given prefix.
4. Delete: Remove a category from the system.
For example, if the system contains refund, refunds, replacement, and return, searching with the prefix ref should return refund and refunds.
The system should efficiently support prefix-based searching without scanning every category.
Use an appropriate data structure and implement the system in Java.

title: Stripe Subscription Notification System – Generate Time-Sorted Email Notifications
description:
Design a subscription notification system that generates email notifications based on users' subscription information and configurable notification schedules.
Each user has subscription information, including an account start date and subscription duration. The system receives notification configurations specifying when emails should be sent.
The notification configurations include:
1. Start: Send an email when the subscription starts.
2. Relative Time: Send an email a specified number of days before or after the subscription end date.
3. End: Send an email when the subscription ends.
The system needs to calculate the absolute sending date for every notification, generate corresponding email events, and return all emails sorted chronologically.
If multiple emails are scheduled for the same date, all events must be preserved.
The implementation should use Java and provide a clean, extensible object-oriented design.

title: Top K Subsets with Maximum Total Weight Using Max Heap and BFS
description:
Given N distinct objects, where each object has a positive integer weight, find the K subsets with the largest total weights.
The subsets should be returned in descending order of their total weights.
Each object can appear at most once in a subset, and different subsets must be unique.
The objective is to avoid generating all 2^N possible subsets when K is relatively small.

title: Move All Ones to the Beginning While Maintaining Relative Order
category: Algorithms / Array Manipulation / Two Pointers / Stable Partition
description:
Given an integer array, move all occurrences of the number 1 to the beginning of the array while maintaining the relative order of all other elements.
The operation must preserve the original relative order of all non-1 elements.
Initially, you may use additional lists to solve the problem. Then, optimize your solution to perform the operation in-place with O(1) extra space.

title: Design a Tool Executor – API Orchestration and Tool Invocation
category: System Design / Object-Oriented Design / API Design / Workflow Orchestration
description:
Design and implement a tool executor that coordinates the execution of external tools.
Given a tool name, the executor must perform the following operations:
1. Retrieve all available tools using GetTools().
2. Find the requested tool by its name.
3. Retrieve the required arguments using GetArguments(tool).
4. Call the external provider using CallProvider(providerId, payload).
5. Return a standardized result object.
The problem provides three helper functions:
GetTools():
Returns a list of all available tools.
GetArguments(tool):
Returns the arguments required by the specified tool.
CallProvider(providerId, payload):
Calls the external provider and returns the execution result.
Important requirements:
- The executor must identify the requested tool.
- The provider ID must be passed as a string.
- The payload must contain both toolName and arguments.
- If the requested tool does not exist, the executor must handle the error.
- Assume GetArguments() and CallProvider() always succeed when the requested tool exists.

title: Aircraft Seating Balance Calculation
description:
You are given a two-dimensional airplane seating layout. Each cell represents a seat or an aisle.
The seating layout uses the following representation:
- X: Empty seat.
- Space: Aisle.
- 1: Passenger with weight category 1.
- 2: Passenger with weight category 2.
- 3: Passenger with weight category 3.
Part 1: Calculate the current center of mass (COM) of the airplane.
Calculate the total passenger weight and the weighted average row and column positions.
The formulas are:
xCOM = Σ(row × weight) / total_weight
yCOM = Σ(col × weight) / total_weight
Use 1-based indexing for both rows and columns.
Part 2: Assign a new passenger to the optimal empty seat.
Given the weight of a new passenger, find the empty seat that minimizes the Euclidean distance between the updated center of mass and the ideal center of the airplane.
The selected seat must:
- Be an empty seat represented by X.
- Minimize the distance between the updated COM and the ideal center.
- Use the same 1-based indexing convention as Part 1.
If no empty seat is available, return an appropriate result.

title: Payment Transaction Fee Calculation
description:
You are given a CSV string containing transaction records from a payment platform. Each transaction contains 10 fields, including transaction ID, transaction status, payment method, and transaction amount.
Your task is to parse the CSV data, calculate the applicable processing fee for each transaction based on its status and payment method, and generate a formatted output string.
The fee calculation rules are:
1. payment_completed:
- Card: 2.1% of the transaction amount + 30 cents.
- Klarna: 2.1% of the transaction amount + 30 cents.
2. dispute_lost:
- All payment methods: 15 cents.
3. dispute_won:
- Klarna: 15 cents.
- Card: 0 cents.
4. Other transaction statuses:
- 0 cents.
The output should contain the transaction ID, transaction type/status, payment method, and calculated fee for each transaction.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
description:
Given a string s, find the length of the longest substring without repeating characters.
A substring is a contiguous sequence of characters within a string.
You need to return the maximum length of a substring in which every character appears only once.

title: 3Sum
description:
Given an integer array nums, return all unique triplets [nums[i], nums[j], nums[k]] such that:
i != j, i != k, and j != k.
nums[i] + nums[j] + nums[k] == 0.
The solution must not contain duplicate triplets.

title: Supervised Learning vs Unsupervised Learning
description:
Explain the differences between supervised learning and unsupervised learning.
Discuss their differences in terms of training data, learning objectives, common algorithms, and real-world applications.

title: Electricity Consumption Aggregation Using SQL
description:
Given two tables, electricity and invoice, calculate the total electricity consumption for each building within its corresponding invoice period.
The electricity table contains individual electricity consumption records, while the invoice table defines the billing period for each building.

title: Copy List with Random Pointer
description:
You are given the head of a special linked list.
Each node contains three fields:
1. val: An integer representing the node's value.
2. next: A pointer to the next node in the linked list.
3. random: A pointer to any node in the linked list or null.
Your task is to create a deep copy of the original linked list.
The copied linked list must contain entirely new nodes. Each copied node must preserve the value and pointer relationships of its corresponding original node.
The next and random pointers in the copied list must point exclusively to copied nodes, never to original nodes.
Return the head of the copied linked list.
The optimized solution should achieve O(n) time complexity and O(1) auxiliary space complexity.

title: Decode String
description:
Given an encoded string containing nested expressions, implement a decoder that expands the string according to the following format:
- Parentheses `()` define a group of characters.
- A repetition count `{k}` immediately follows the closing parenthesis.
- The characters inside the parentheses must be repeated exactly `k` times.
- Groups can be nested to arbitrary valid depths.
- Any character outside the structural delimiters is treated as a literal character.
- Empty groups and multi-digit repetition counts are allowed.
Unlike the traditional Decode String problem, which uses the format `k[encoded_string]`, this problem uses `(encoded_string){k}`.
Your task is to decode the entire input string and return the expanded result.
The input is guaranteed to have valid parentheses and repetition-count syntax. You do not need to handle malformed expressions.

title: Group Anagrams (Hash Map Optimization)
description:
Given an array of strings, group all anagrams together. Anagrams are strings that contain the same characters with the same frequencies but may appear in different orders.
You can return the groups in any order.

title: ExamTracker Class Design (Prefix Sum and Range Query)
description:
Design an ExamTracker class that supports recording examination scores and querying the total score within a given time interval.
The class should implement three methods:
1. __init__(): Initialize the ExamTracker.
2. record(time, score): Record an examination score at a specific time.
3. totalScore(startTime, endTime): Return the total score of all examinations recorded within the inclusive time interval [startTime, endTime].
The problem guarantees that record() is called with strictly increasing timestamps.

title: Box Storage Problem
role: PhD University Grad Machine Learning Engineer 2026 (US)
description:
You are given two arrays:
- shelf_height: An array representing the heights of shelf positions.
- box_height: An array representing the heights of boxes, sorted in ascending order.
Boxes enter the shelf from the left side. Each box must pass through all preceding shelf positions before reaching its target position.
If a box's height exceeds the height of a shelf position, the box gets stuck and blocks access to subsequent positions.
Each shelf position can hold at most one box.
Your task is to determine the maximum number of boxes that can be successfully placed on the shelves.
Core Rules:
1. Each shelf position can hold at most one box.
2. Boxes must enter from left to right.
3. Each box must pass through all preceding shelf positions.
4. If a box is taller than a shelf position, it gets stuck and prevents access to subsequent positions.
5. The box_height array is already sorted in ascending order.

title: Count Opposite Pairs Using Hash Map Frequency Counting
role: Software Engineer / Software Development Engineer (SDE I / SDE II)
description:
Given an integer array, find the total number of pairs whose elements are opposites of each other.
Two integers x and -x form an opposite pair. Each array element can only be used once.
You need to implement two functions:
1. countOppositePairs(): Return the total number of valid opposite pairs.
2. getOppositePairs(): Return all valid pairs as a vector of pairs.
Important conditions:
- Each element can only be used once.
- Duplicate numbers are allowed.
- Zero is its own opposite and must be paired with another zero.
- Each pair should only be counted once.
- The order of returned pairs does not matter.

title: Thread-Safe Ring Buffer with Batch Read and Write Operations
description:
Design and implement a fixed-capacity Ring Buffer (Circular Buffer) that supports batch write and batch read operations.
The Ring Buffer follows the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle. Elements are read in the same order in which they were written.
The buffer must support the following operations:
1. create(capacity): Initialize a Ring Buffer with a fixed capacity.
2. write(items): Write multiple elements into the buffer and return the number of successfully written elements.
3. read(count): Read and remove up to count elements from the buffer, returning them in FIFO order.
Important requirements:
- The buffer has a fixed capacity.
- Each write operation can only insert elements into available slots.
- If the buffer is full, new elements must be rejected rather than overwriting existing elements.
- When the tail reaches the end of the underlying array, it wraps around to the beginning.
- Reading must always return the oldest available elements first.
- If the requested read count exceeds the current number of elements, return all available elements.
- Reading from an empty buffer should return an empty collection.
- The implementation should maintain correct behavior when multiple threads access the buffer concurrently.

title: Binary Search Tree Range Sum with Pruning
description:
Given the root of a Binary Search Tree (BST) and two integers `low` and `high`, return the sum of all node values within the inclusive range `[low, high]`.
A Binary Search Tree satisfies the following properties:
- All values in the left subtree are smaller than the current node's value.
- All values in the right subtree are greater than the current node's value.
The goal is to calculate the range sum efficiently by leveraging the BST properties instead of traversing every node unnecessarily.

title: Merge Two Sorted Interval Lists Using Two Pointers
description:
Given two sorted lists of non-overlapping intervals, merge them into a single sorted list representing their union.
Each interval is represented as `[start, end]`.
Both input lists are already sorted by their starting values, and intervals within each individual list do not overlap.
The resulting list must satisfy the following requirements:
- Include every interval from both input lists.
- Merge overlapping intervals into a single interval.
- Maintain ascending order based on starting values.
- Handle cases where one input list becomes empty before the other.
- Avoid modifying the original input intervals.
The key challenge is to merge two already-sorted interval lists efficiently without sorting all intervals again.

title: Populating Next Right Pointers in an Arbitrary Binary Tree
description:
Given the root of a binary tree, each node contains three pointers: `left`, `right`, and `next`.
The `left` and `right` pointers represent the node's children, while the `next` pointer should point to the node immediately to its right at the same level.
Your task is to populate the `next` pointer of every node so that all nodes at the same level are connected from left to right.
If there is no node to the right at the same level, its `next` pointer should be set to `null`.
Unlike a perfect binary tree, the given tree may have missing left or right children.
The solution must correctly handle arbitrary binary tree structures.

title: 132 Pattern Detection Using a Monotonic Stack
description:
Given an integer array `orders`, determine whether there exist three indices `i`, `j`, and `k` satisfying:
\[i < j < k\] and \[orders[i] < orders[k] < orders[j]\]
This pattern is known as a **132 Pattern**.
The three elements form the following relationship:
- `orders[i]`: The smallest value (1).
- `orders[j]`: The largest value (3).
- `orders[k]`: The middle value (2).
The goal is to determine whether at least one such triple exists.
This problem is a variation of LeetCode 456, 132 Pattern.
**Follow-up extensions:**
1. Explain why the monotonic stack solution achieves O(n) time complexity.
2. Analyze the worst-case auxiliary space complexity.
3. Extend the solution to return the actual triple `(i_val, j_val, k_val)`.
4. If multiple triples exist, return one with the smallest possible starting index `i`.
5. Implement a simplified version that returns any valid triple.

title: Design a Calendar API with Sorted Event Retrieval
description:
Design a Calendar class that supports adding events and retrieving all scheduled events.
Each event contains three attributes:
- `start`: Event start time.
- `end`: Event end time.
- `name`: Event name.
The Calendar class must support two operations:
1. `add_event(start, end, name)`: Add a new event to the calendar.
2. `get_events()`: Return all events sorted by start time, then end time, and finally event name.
The interviewer expects a clean implementation that takes advantage of Python's built-in sorting behavior.

title: Optimizing Calendar API for Read-Heavy Workloads
category: Data Structures / API Design / Performance Optimization
description:
Starting from the basic Calendar implementation, optimize the system for a read-heavy workload.
Assume that `get_events()` is called approximately ten times more frequently than `add_event()`.
The original implementation sorts all events every time `get_events()` is called, resulting in O(n log n) retrieval time.
The requirement is to optimize `get_events()` to achieve O(1) time complexity.
The expected approach is to move the sorting and formatting costs from the read operation to the write operation.
The Calendar class should support:
1. `add_event(start, end, name)`: Insert a new event while maintaining sorted order.
2. `get_events()`: Return the already-sorted event collection without sorting again.
The interviewer also explores the trade-offs between returning a list and a tuple, as well as the consequences of returning references to mutable internal objects.

title: Calendar Interval Overlap Detection
description:
Extend the Calendar class by implementing an interval overlap query.
Given a query interval:
[start, end)
Return all existing calendar events that overlap with the query interval.
Each event contains:
- `start`: Event starting time.
- `end`: Event ending time.
- `name`: Event name.
The interviewer focuses particularly on how to define interval overlap correctly.
Instead of enumerating every possible overlapping configuration, derive the conditions under which two intervals do NOT overlap, then negate those conditions.
For two intervals A and B, they do not overlap if:
1. A ends before or exactly when B starts.
2. B ends before or exactly when A starts.
Therefore, the overlap condition is:
A_end > B_start and B_end > A_start
The implementation should extract this logic into a reusable helper function.

title: Bilateral Trade Compression Using HashMap
category: Data Structures / HashMap / Financial Transaction Processing
description:
Design and implement a transaction compression algorithm that consolidates multiple financial transactions between trading parties.
Each transaction contains five attributes:
- `tradingParty`: The party initiating the transaction.
- `counterParty`: The other party involved in the transaction.
- `amount`: The transaction amount.
- `currency`: The transaction currency.
- `timestamp`: The transaction timestamp.
The objective is to calculate the final net exposure between every pair of parties for each currency.
Transactions can occur in opposite directions. For example:
- A → D: 100 USD
- D → A: 40 USD
These two transactions should be compressed into a single transaction:
- A → D: 60 USD
The algorithm must process the input transaction list in one pass using a HashMap.
The aggregation key must identify both parties and the currency. Transaction direction must be represented by the sign of the accumulated amount.
The final output should contain only non-zero compressed transactions.
**Core requirements:**
1. Define an appropriate transaction data structure.
2. Aggregate transactions by party pair and currency.
3. Handle opposite transaction directions correctly.
4. Normalize party pairs to avoid duplicate keys.
5. Produce compressed transactions from the final net balances.
6. Achieve O(n) expected time complexity.

title: Maximum Reward Job Scheduling with Deadlines
category: Greedy Algorithms / Heap / Priority Queue / Job Scheduling
description:
You are given a collection of jobs, where each job has two attributes:
- `deadline`: The latest time slot by which the job must be completed.
- `reward`: The reward earned if the job is successfully completed.
Each job takes exactly one unit of time, and only one job can be executed in each time slot.
Your objective is to select a subset of jobs that maximizes the total reward while ensuring that every selected job can be completed before or at its deadline.
The interview focuses on designing a greedy scheduling algorithm using priority queues and determining whether the selected tasks are guaranteed to be optimal.
A reward-first greedy strategy may appear to work on simple test cases but can produce incorrect results because selecting a high-reward job first does not necessarily preserve the feasibility of other jobs.
The optimal approach is to:
1. Sort jobs by deadline in ascending order.
2. Iterate through the jobs and insert their rewards into a min heap.
3. If the number of selected jobs exceeds the current deadline, remove the job with the smallest reward.
4. Calculate the sum of the remaining rewards.
The algorithm achieves O(n log n) time complexity.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array with Duplicates
category: Binary Search / Array / Divide and Conquer
description:
You are given an integer array `nums` that was originally sorted in ascending order and then rotated at an unknown pivot. Your task is to determine whether a given target value exists in the array.
The array may contain distinct elements in the original version of the problem. A follow-up allows duplicate elements.
You must achieve O(log n) time complexity when all elements are distinct.
When duplicate elements are allowed, the algorithm must handle situations where it is impossible to determine which half is sorted. In such cases, the search range must be reduced carefully, and the worst-case time complexity may degrade to O(n).
The key idea is to identify which half of the current search range is sorted and determine whether the target belongs to that half.

title: Priority-Based Task Scheduler with Dependencies
category: Graph / Topological Sorting / Priority Queue / Heap / API Design / Task Scheduling
description:
Design and implement a Task Scheduler class that supports registering tasks with priorities and dependencies, and executing them in the correct order.
Each task contains:
- A unique task ID.
- An integer priority.
- A list of dependencies representing tasks that must be completed before this task can execute.
The scheduler must support the following operations:
**1. addTask(taskId, priority, dependencies)**
Register a new task with its priority and dependencies.
**2. runAllTasks()**
Execute all registered tasks while satisfying the following rules:
- A task cannot execute until all its dependencies have been completed.
- Among all currently executable tasks, always execute the task with the highest priority.
- Once a task finishes, update the dependency status of its dependent tasks.
- Newly available tasks must immediately become candidates for execution.
- If a circular dependency exists, raise an exception during runAllTasks().
**3. runTask(taskId)**
Execute an individual task. For this interview problem, execution can be represented by printing its task ID.
The scheduler must return or output the task IDs in their actual execution order.
The central challenge is combining dependency management with priority-based scheduling. Sorting all tasks by priority is insufficient because dependency constraints must always take precedence.

title: Reorder Linked List
description:
Given the head of a singly linked list, reorder the list so that its nodes alternate between the beginning and the end of the original list.
The reordering must follow this pattern:
- Take the first node.
- Take the last node.
- Take the second node.
- Take the second-to-last node.
- Continue alternating until all nodes have been used.
The original node values must remain unchanged. Only the links between nodes should be modified.
You must perform the reordering in place without creating additional data structures proportional to the input size.

title: Topological Sort – Dependency-Based Execution Order
description:
Given a set of tasks and their dependency relationships, determine a valid execution order that satisfies all dependencies.
A task can only be executed after all its prerequisite tasks have been completed.
The problem can be modeled as a directed graph:
- Each task represents a vertex.
- Each dependency represents a directed edge from the prerequisite task to the dependent task.
- The resulting execution order must satisfy every dependency.
The objective is to return a valid ordering of all tasks.

title: Greedy Order Batching
description:
Given a list of delivery orders, each order contains an order ID, merchant ID, and pickup time.
Your task is to group orders into batches while satisfying the following constraints:
1. Orders in the same batch must belong to the same merchant.
2. Each batch cannot exceed the maximum capacity.
3. The difference between the earliest and latest pickup times in a batch cannot exceed the specified time window.
4. Every order must be assigned to exactly one batch.
5. Minimize the total number of batches.
Implement an algorithm to generate the batches while satisfying all constraints.

title: Minimum-Sum 3×3 Submatrix with No-Zero Constraint
description:
Given an n × m matrix representing water consumption values, find the 3×3 submatrix with the minimum total water consumption.
The submatrix must:
- Contain exactly 3 rows and 3 columns.
- Stay completely within the matrix boundaries.
- Have the minimum possible sum among all valid 3×3 submatrices.
Follow-up requirement:
Modify the algorithm so that a valid 3×3 submatrix cannot contain any zero values.
Return the minimum sum and the top-left coordinates of the selected submatrix. If no valid submatrix exists, return None.

title: 2D Range Sum Query – 2D Prefix Sum
description:
Given a 2D matrix of integers, implement a function that efficiently calculates the sum of elements inside a rectangular region.
The query is defined by four coordinates:
- row1: Starting row
- col1: Starting column
- row2: Ending row
- col2: Ending column
Both boundaries are inclusive.
The goal is to preprocess the matrix so that each range sum query can be answered in O(1) time.

title: Maximum Score Path in a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG)
description:
You are given a directed acyclic graph (DAG) containing `n` nodes and a list of directed edges.
Each node has an associated score, and each directed edge has an associated cost.
You are also given a starting node `start`.
Your task is to find a path starting from `start` and ending at any reachable node such that the total path score is maximized.
The total path score is calculated as:
- Add the scores of all nodes included in the path.
- Subtract the costs of all edges used in the path.
You must return both the maximum achievable score and the corresponding path.
The path must follow the direction of the edges. You cannot visit a node unless it is reachable from the starting node through valid directed edges.
The graph is guaranteed to be a DAG, so a valid topological ordering exists.
The implementation should also handle unreachable nodes correctly and reconstruct the actual path using parent pointers.

title: Greedy Word Wrapping with Exact Box Formatting
description:
Given a list of text paragraphs and a fixed content width, format all text into a rectangular text box and return the formatted output.
Each paragraph consists of words separated by whitespace. You must wrap the text according to the following rules:
1. Words must remain intact and cannot be split across multiple lines.
2. Each output content line must contain at most the specified width of characters.
3. Words should be packed greedily: add as many consecutive words as possible to the current line without exceeding the width.
4. When the next word cannot fit, finish the current line and start a new line with that word.
5. Each paragraph must preserve its original order.
6. Consecutive paragraphs must be separated by one empty content line.
7. The entire output must be enclosed in a rectangular border.
8. The top and bottom borders should appear exactly once.
9. Every content line must have the same width, with spaces added to the right when necessary.
10. The function should return the formatted lines instead of printing internally, allowing the caller to control console output.
The content width does not include the border characters or the padding spaces surrounding the content.

title: DMA Interrupt Data Transfer Using a Lock-Free Ring Buffer
category: Embedded Systems / Concurrent Programming / Data Structures
description:
You are given an embedded system where a DMA controller continuously transfers data from a hardware device into memory. Whenever a DMA transfer completes, an interrupt service routine (ISR) is triggered, and the ISR communicates the received sample to the CPU main loop through shared memory.
The original implementation uses a single shared variable to store the latest sample.
However, when DMA produces multiple samples before the CPU consumes them, earlier samples can be overwritten. For example, if the producer generates A, B, C, D, the CPU may only observe some of the samples rather than receiving all four in order.
Your task is to analyze the original implementation and redesign the data transfer mechanism so that the CPU can consume samples reliably without losing data under normal operating conditions.
The expected solution is a Single Producer Single Consumer (SPSC) Ring Buffer.
The shared variable only stores the latest value. If the producer updates it multiple times before the consumer reads it, intermediate samples can be overwritten.

title: A/B/C Message Matching
description:
You are given a sequence of interleaved messages from multiple clients. Each client sends exactly three types of messages in order: A → B → C.
Messages A and C contain a client ID, but message B does not contain a client ID.
Your task is to reconstruct the missing client ID for every B message while preserving the original message order.
The input is guaranteed to be valid. Messages from different clients can be interleaved, and the ordering guarantees allow us to match messages using FIFO queues.
You need to assign each B message the client ID of the client who sent it.

title: Connected Crop Grid Construction
description:
Given an N × M grid and K different crops, each crop has a specified number of cells that it must occupy.
The sum of all crop counts equals N × M.
Your task is to construct any valid grid such that all cells belonging to the same crop form one connected component.
Connectivity is defined using four directions: up, down, left, and right. Diagonal adjacency does not count.

title: CPU Process Scheduling — FCFS and Priority Scheduling
description:
You are given a list of processes. Each process has a submission time (arrival time) and an execution time (burst time).
Implement a CPU scheduling algorithm that calculates the start time and completion time of every process.
Part 1: FCFS (First Come, First Served)
Processes must execute in ascending order of submission time. If multiple processes arrive at the same time, use their original input order.
Part 2: Priority Scheduling (Follow-up)
Extend the scheduling algorithm by introducing a priority value for each process. A smaller priority number represents a higher priority.
The CPU should always select the highest-priority process among all processes that have already arrived.
The scheduling policy is non-preemptive, meaning once a process starts executing, it cannot be interrupted by a newly arriving process.
If multiple eligible processes have the same priority, select the one with the earlier submission time. If both are equal, use original input order.

title: Fibonacci Tree – Shortest Path Between Two Labeled Nodes
description:
Given a Fibonacci Tree of order n, each node is assigned a unique integer label according to preorder traversal.
Given two node labels, start and end, return the shortest path between them using the following directions:
- U: Move to the parent.
- L: Move to the left child.
- R: Move to the right child.
The Fibonacci Tree is defined recursively:
- T0 and T1 each contain one node.
- For n >= 2, Tn consists of a root, a left subtree T(n-1), and a right subtree T(n-2).
The number of nodes grows exponentially with the tree order. Therefore, explicitly constructing the entire tree is inefficient.
The follow-up questions extend the problem to complexity analysis, direct navigation without constructing the tree, LCA-based path reconstruction, and postorder labeling.

title: Streaming Data Compression with RLE and Bit-Packing
description:
Design a streaming data compression system that supports two encoding strategies: Run-Length Encoding (RLE) and Bit Packing (BP).
The system receives input values incrementally through a write method and produces compressed output through a get_data method.
The implementation must satisfy the following requirements:
1. The system must process incoming values incrementally rather than storing the entire input sequence in memory.
2. RLE should have priority over BP whenever the input satisfies the RLE encoding conditions.
3. Every non-final BP run must contain at least 8 values.
4. A BP run containing fewer than 8 values cannot be finalized in the middle of the stream. It must be forward-merged according to the encoding rules.
5. The final run has a special exception and may contain fewer than 8 values.
6. The get_data method must correctly flush the remaining buffered values and apply the final-run exception.
The main challenge is determining when a run can safely be finalized without violating the encoding rules.

title: Large-Scale Tweet Search Using Inverted Index
category: Data Structures / Search Optimization / Algorithm Design
description:
Design an efficient search system for a large collection of tweets.
Each tweet contains a unique ID and a text string. Given a search query containing one or more words, return the top 10 most relevant tweets.
The relevance of a tweet is determined by the number of distinct query words appearing in that tweet.
A tweet containing more matching query words should receive a higher score.
The initial brute-force approach scans every tweet and calculates its relevance score. However, this approach becomes inefficient when the dataset grows to millions of tweets.
Design an optimized solution using an inverted index so that each query only processes tweets associated with the search terms.
The system should also support incremental updates when new tweets arrive, without rebuilding the entire index.

title: Cheapest Common Ancestor
category: Data Structures / Tree / Parent Pointer / Hash Set
description:
Given two nodes in a tree, find the common ancestor with the lowest price.
Each node contains:
- A unique identifier.
- A price.
- A pointer to its parent.
A common ancestor is a node that appears in the parent chain of both input nodes. The node itself can also be considered an ancestor of itself.
Return the common ancestor with the minimum price.
If multiple common ancestors have the same minimum price, returning any one of them is acceptable.
If the two nodes belong to different trees and have no common ancestor, return None.

title: Multi-Path IP-Based Rate Limiter
category: System Design / Data Structures / Rate Limiting
description:
Design a rate limiter that supports different request limits for different HTTP paths.
For example:
- `/foo`: Each IP address can make at most 3 requests per minute.
- `/bar`: Each IP address can make at most 5 requests per minute.
The rate limiter must independently track requests based on the combination of client IP address and HTTP path.
For example, requests from the same IP to `/foo` and `/bar` must have separate counters. Similarly, two different IP addresses accessing the same path must also have independent counters.
Implement a rate limiter that determines whether an incoming request should be allowed or rejected.
The system should support:
1. Different rate limits for different HTTP paths.
2. Independent request tracking for each IP-path combination.
3. Sliding time windows.
4. Correct handling of expired requests.
5. Thread-safe request processing.

title: Payment and Invoice Matching
description:
Design a payment-to-invoice matching system that supports two different matching strategies: memo-based matching and amount-based matching.
Given a list of invoices and a list of payments, determine which invoice should be matched with each payment.
The system must follow these matching rules:
1. Memo-Based Matching: If a payment contains an explicit invoice ID in its memo, match the payment directly to that invoice.
2. Amount-Based Matching: If the payment does not contain an invoice ID, find an unmatched invoice with the same amount.
3. Priority Matching: When multiple unmatched invoices have the same amount, select the invoice with the earliest due date.
4. Each invoice can only be matched to one payment.
5. If no eligible invoice exists, return None for that payment.
The goal is to implement an efficient matching algorithm that handles both matching strategies while maintaining the correct priority.

title: Word Search – DFS and Backtracking
description:
Given an m × n character matrix and a target string, determine whether the target string can be constructed by sequentially moving through adjacent cells.
You can move in four directions: up, down, left, and right.
Each cell can only be used once in a single search path.
Return true if the target string exists in the matrix; otherwise, return false.

title: Maximum Number of Nodes at Any Tree Level – BFS Level Order Traversal
description:
Given the root of a tree, return the level index containing the maximum number of nodes.
The root node is at level 0, and each subsequent level increases by one.
If multiple levels contain the same maximum number of nodes, return the smallest level index.
If the tree is empty, return -1.

title: Add Two Numbers II – Forward Order Linked List Addition
description:
You are given two non-empty singly linked lists representing two non-negative integers.
The digits are stored in forward order, meaning the most significant digit comes first.
Each node contains a single digit from 0 to 9.
Add the two numbers and return the result as a linked list, also in forward order.
You cannot assume that the two linked lists have the same length.
The main challenge is that addition must start from the least significant digit, but the linked lists can only be traversed from head to tail.

title: Inline String Truncation in JSX
description:
Given a string, display it in a JSX component.
If the string exceeds a specified maximum length, truncate it and append "..." to the end.
Otherwise, display the original string.
Implement this logic directly inside JSX using a JavaScript expression.

title: Fixing Missing Parameter Types in TypeScript
description:
You are implementing a JavaScript or TypeScript function, but the compiler reports an error because one or more function parameters do not have explicit types.
Explain how to resolve the error by adding appropriate parameter types.
You should also understand when using any is acceptable as a temporary workaround and why explicit types are generally preferred.

title: Anagram Index – Find the First Anagram Occurrence in a String
description:
Given two strings, text and query, find the starting index of the first substring in text that is an anagram of query.
An anagram is a string that contains exactly the same characters with the same frequencies, but potentially in a different order.
The substring must have exactly the same length as query.
Return the starting index of the first matching substring. If no matching substring exists, return -1.
The solution should use a sliding window and character frequency tracking to avoid comparing two dictionaries at every window position.

title: Design a Pricing Service with Hard and Soft Dependencies
category: System Design / Backend Engineering / Fault Tolerance
description:
Design a Pricing Service that integrates two downstream services: Cart API and Promotions API.
The service needs to retrieve cart information, calculate the base price, apply available promotions, and return the final price to the customer.
The system must handle failures from downstream dependencies correctly.
The key requirements are:
1. Cart API provides essential cart information and is a hard dependency. If it fails, the Pricing Service must fail fast rather than calculate an incorrect price.
2. Promotions API provides optional discount information and is a soft dependency. If it fails, the system should gracefully degrade and continue checkout using the base price.
3. The system must distinguish between an API returning an unsuccessful HTTP status code and an API call failing entirely due to timeout, connection errors, or other exceptions.
4. The system must provide observability through metrics and logging so engineers can identify when fallback logic is executed.
5. The implementation should preserve checkout availability without silently hiding downstream failures.

title: Order Batching with Merchant Isolation, Time Windows, and Capacity Constraints
description:
Given a list of orders, each order contains a merchant_id and a pickup_time.
Design an algorithm to minimize the total number of batches (trips) while satisfying the following constraints:
1. Orders from different merchants cannot be placed in the same batch.
2. All orders in one batch must have pickup times within the time window [t0, t0 + W], where t0 is the earliest pickup time in that batch.
3. Each batch can contain at most B orders.
4. Every order must belong to exactly one batch.
5. Return both the minimum number of batches and the actual order groupings using their original input indices.
The goal is to minimize the total number of batches while satisfying all constraints.

title: Build hierarchical descriptions using indentation levels.
description:
Given a list of records already sorted in hierarchical order, each record contains an `indent` level and a `description`.
Generate an `Aggregated Description` for every record by combining its own description with all non-empty descriptions from its ancestors, separated by `" / "`.
Requirements:
1. Records are already ordered correctly. Do not sort them.
2. The indentation level represents the record's position in the hierarchy.
3. Empty descriptions must be excluded from the aggregated string.
4. Empty descriptions must still occupy their original structural level.
5. Moving to a shallower indentation level must remove all deeper levels from the current path.

title: Debug Node.js module resolution errors.
description:
While running a provided `starter.js` file, Node.js reports:
`Error: Cannot find module`
Identify the root cause and determine whether the issue comes from an incorrect file path, a missing dependency, or an incorrect module import.
The objective is to diagnose the problem efficiently without unnecessarily modifying application logic.

title: Calculate monthly warehouse shipment totals using LEFT JOIN.
description:
Given two tables:
| warehouse_id | warehouse_name |
|---|---|
| 1 | North |
| 2 | South |
| 3 | East |
| shipment_id | warehouse_id | shipped_at | quantity |
|---|---|---|---|
| 101 | 1 | 2025-01-05 | 300 |
| 102 | 1 | 2025-01-20 | 250 |
| 103 | 2 | 2025-01-10 | 400 |
| 104 | 3 | 2024-12-31 | 900 |

Write a SQL query to calculate the total shipment quantity for each warehouse during January 2025.
Requirements:
1. Include all warehouses in the initial aggregation, even if they have no shipments.
2. Only count shipments occurring in January 2025.
3. Calculate the total shipment quantity for each warehouse.
4. Return only warehouses whose total shipment quantity is greater than 500.
5. Preserve warehouses as the primary table.

title: Implement tail to efficiently retrieve the last N lines of a large file.
description:
Implement the Unix `tail` functionality that returns the last N lines of a file.
The file may be extremely large, so loading the entire file into memory is not acceptable. You do not need to be familiar with any specific file-reading API; focus on designing an efficient algorithm.
The implementation should support two approaches:
1. Forward Reading: Read the file line by line and maintain only the last N lines using a deque or circular buffer.
2. Backward Reading: Start from the end of the file and read backward in fixed-size blocks, counting newline characters until the last N lines are located.
The optimized solution should minimize unnecessary I/O operations and memory consumption.

title: Amazon Locker System Design
description:
Design an Amazon Locker system that manages lockers, packages, and hubs.
The system should support the following operations:
1. A Hub manages multiple lockers.
2. Each Locker has a unique locker ID and can store at most one package.
3. A Package has a unique package ID.
4. When a package arrives, the system assigns it to an available locker.
5. Customers can pick up packages from their assigned lockers.
6. Once a package is picked up, the corresponding locker becomes available again.
The main objective is to design clear object responsibilities and maintain consistent package and locker states.

title: Currency Conversion Using Graphs
description:
Design a Currency Conversion system that supports converting amounts between different currencies.
The system should support the following operations:
1. Register exchange rates between two currencies.
2. Represent currencies as graph nodes.
3. Represent exchange rates as weighted edges.
4. Calculate the conversion rate between two currencies by finding a path in the graph.
5. Multiply exchange rates along the path to obtain the final conversion rate.
6. Return an appropriate result when no conversion path exists.
For example, if:
USD → GBP = 0.8
GBP → EUR = 1.1
Then:
USD → EUR = 0.8 × 1.1 = 0.88
Assumptions:
1. Exchange rates are positive.
2. Reverse conversion rates are reciprocal.
3. For this basic implementation, any valid conversion path is acceptable.
4. If multiple paths produce different rates, the business rule for selecting a path must be clarified.

title: Calculate Login Time Under Password Lockout Rules
description:
Given a list of distinct password strings, one of which is the correct password, calculate the minimum and maximum time required to successfully log in.
The password attempts follow these rules:
1. Passwords must be attempted in non-decreasing order of string length.
2. Passwords with the same length can be attempted in any order.
3. Each password attempt takes exactly 1 second.
4. After every k failed attempts, the system imposes a 5-second lockout before the next attempt.
5. The process ends immediately when the correct password is entered.
Return the minimum and maximum possible login times.
The key observation is that all passwords shorter than the correct password must be attempted first, while passwords of the same length can be arranged to produce the best or worst outcome.

title: Synonym Group Replacement Using Union-Find
description:
Given a list of synonym pairs and a sequence of words representing a code snippet, group words that are synonyms and replace each word with the representative of its synonym group.
Two words belong to the same group if they are directly or indirectly connected through synonym relationships.
Each group must have one representative word, selected according to the following rules:
1. Choose the shortest word in the group.
2. If multiple words have the same shortest length, choose the word that appeared earliest.
After constructing all synonym groups, replace every word in the original code sequence with its group's representative.
Words that do not belong to any synonym group should remain unchanged.
The key challenge is implementing Union-Find while keeping the structural root independent from the business-level representative word.

title: Group Anagrams Using Character Frequency Counting
description:
Given an array of strings, group all anagrams together.
Two strings are considered anagrams if they contain exactly the same characters with the same frequencies, regardless of their character order.
Return a list of groups where each group contains all strings that are anagrams of each other.
The order of the groups does not need to be specified unless explicitly required.

title: Optimal Card-Picking Strategy
description:
You are given an array of integers representing the values of a row of cards.
Two players take turns picking exactly one card from either the left or right end of the remaining array. Each player wants to maximize their own total score, and both players play optimally.
Player 1 always goes first. The game continues until all cards have been picked.
Implement a function that returns the maximum total score Player 1 can achieve, assuming both players play optimally.

title: Appointment Search and Ranking
description:
You are implementing an appointment recommendation feature for a healthcare scheduling system.
The system provides a list of available appointments. Each appointment contains information such as its appointment type, start time, location, and provider.
Implement two functions:
1. Find the earliest available appointment for a given appointment type.
2. Filter appointments based on a specified time window and location, then sort the matching appointments by start time.
The implementation should prioritize simplicity and correctness. Avoid unnecessary system design or over-engineering.

title: Course Scheduling – Minimum Completion Time Using Topological Sort
description:
Given a set of courses with different completion durations and a list of prerequisite dependencies, calculate the minimum total time required to complete all courses.
Multiple courses can be completed simultaneously as long as their prerequisite dependencies are satisfied.
A course can only start after all its prerequisite courses have been completed. The goal is to find the minimum time required to finish every course.
The key is to recognize that this is a longest path problem on a Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), rather than simply summing all course durations.

title: Meeting Rooms II – Minimum Number of Meeting Rooms
description:
Given a list of meeting time intervals, where each interval is represented as `[start, end]`, determine the minimum number of meeting rooms required to accommodate all meetings without conflicts.
Two meetings cannot use the same room if their time intervals overlap. A meeting ending at the exact time another meeting starts does not require an additional room.
The goal is to calculate the maximum number of simultaneously ongoing meetings.

title: Grid BFS with Gas Constraints and Obstacles
description:
Given a 2D grid representing a map, determine whether a car can reach a destination called an oasis.
Initially, the problem is a standard grid BFS problem. The car starts at a given position and can move up, down, left, or right to reach the oasis.
The interviewer then introduces additional constraints:
- Certain cells contain rocks that cannot be traversed.
- Every movement consumes one unit of gas.
- Gas stations allow the car to replenish its gas.
- The car has a maximum gas capacity.
- The algorithm must prevent infinite loops caused by revisiting locations.
The challenge is to extend the original BFS solution to account for remaining gas while avoiding unnecessary repeated exploration.
For the implementation, assume visiting a gas station refills the tank to its maximum capacity.

title: Reach the Oasis with Limited Fuel
description:
You are given a 2D grid representing a map. A car starts at a given position and needs to reach a destination called the oasis.
Initially, determine whether the car can reach the oasis using grid traversal. The interviewer may progressively introduce additional constraints, including rocks and gas stations.
The car can move in four directions: up, down, left, and right. Each movement consumes one unit of gas. The car cannot move through rocks. When entering a gas station, the car refills its tank.
Your task is to determine whether the car can reach the oasis while respecting all movement, obstacle, and fuel constraints.
Assumption for this reconstructed version: entering a gas station refills the tank to its maximum capacity. Confirm the exact refueling rule with the interviewer.

title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals, where each interval contains a start time and an end time, determine the minimum number of meeting rooms required to accommodate all meetings.
Two meetings cannot use the same room if their time intervals overlap.
Return the minimum number of rooms needed to schedule all meetings without conflicts.

title: Remove Stars From a String
description:
Given a string containing regular characters and asterisks (*), process the string according to the following rule: whenever an asterisk appears, it removes the closest non-removed character to its left.
Return the resulting string after processing all characters.
The relative order of the remaining characters must be preserved.

title: Minimum Meeting Rooms
description:
Given an array of meeting time intervals, where each interval contains a start time and an end time, determine the minimum number of meeting rooms required to accommodate all meetings.
Two meetings cannot use the same room if their time intervals overlap.
Return the minimum number of rooms needed to schedule all meetings without conflicts.

title: Top consumer in Every city
description:
Suppose there are two tables: user_info and order_info.
The user_info table stores basic information about users, including:
- user_id: The unique ID of each user.
- city: The city where the user is located.
- reg_time: The registration time of the user.
The order_info table stores order information, including:
- order_id: The unique ID of each order.
- user_id: The ID of the user who placed the order, associated with user_info.user_id.
- order_amount: The amount of the order.
- order_time: The time when the order was placed.
Find the top consumer in every city based on the total order amount spent by each user.
If multiple users in the same city have the same highest total spending, return all of them.

title: Implement Vector Dot Product
description:
Implement the dot product of two one-dimensional vectors without using built-in dot product functions.
Given two vectors a and b of equal length, calculate their dot product by multiplying corresponding elements and summing the results.
The mathematical definition is:
dot(a, b) = Σ(a[i] * b[i])
The implementation should use PyTorch tensor operations and explain potential floating-point precision issues.

title: Reshape and Split Query and Key Tensors
description:
Given an input tensor with shape [B, S, D], split it into Query (Q) and Key (K) tensors for multi-head attention.
The hidden dimension D contains information for the number of attention heads, the Q/K dimension, and the head dimension.
Reshape the tensor to separate these dimensions, split Query and Key, and rearrange the dimensions into the expected multi-head attention format.
Assume the input packs Q and K in the order [Q, K] along the last dimension.

title: Implement Patchify Without Rearrange
description:
Given an image tensor with shape [B, C, H, W], implement a patchify operation without using einops.rearrange().
Divide the image into non-overlapping patches of size P × P.
Move the spatial patch dimensions into the channel dimension, producing a space-to-depth transformation.
The output tensor should have shape:
[B, C * P * P, H / P, W / P]

title: Sort Data Using Argsort and Gather
description:
Given a key tensor and a data tensor, sort the data according to the corresponding key values.
The data tensor has shape [B, S, D], while the key tensor has shape [B, S].
First, calculate the sorting indices using argsort().
Then use gather() to reorder the data tensor along the sequence dimension.
The implementation should explain why unsqueeze() and expand() are needed to make the index tensor compatible with gather().
